statement: In setting (S), let $R$ be a unital ring. Write $\mathcal I_M$ for the directed poset of nonempty finite strong subsets of $M$, with inclusions. For $V:A_M\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ put $S_RV=\operatorname{colim}_{B\in\mathcal I_M}V(B)$. This is a smooth $R[G]$-module under \[ g\,[B,v]=[gB,V(g|_B)v]. \] The functor $S_R$ is exact, and naturally \[ \operatorname{colim}_{A_M}V\cong(S_RV)_G. \] Consequently $\operatorname{colim}_{A}$ is exact over $R$ if and only if coinvariants preserve monomorphisms of smooth $R[G]$-modules. In particular, exactness over a specified ring depends only on the topological group $G$, not on its chosen strong Fra\"iss\'e presentation. No rigidity, strong-amalgamation, or functorial-amalgamation hypothesis is needed here.
notes: Proved: Lead 1

statement: In setting (S), the following are equivalent: amenability of $G$; the finite-function convex Ramsey property stated in R12(ii), with every embedding required to be strong; (Re); and (CC). Rigidity is not required. The convex Ramsey statement is Moore's Theorem~7.1(5)--(6) in the published paper, numbered Theorem~6.1 in the supplied arXiv source, for ordinary ages; the proof below establishes the strong version directly, rather than treating cofinality as a transfer theorem \cite{ABMoore2013}.
notes: Proved: Lead 2, including the strong-class passage

statement: In setting (S) with (Rig), \[ \mathrm{(CH)}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ is Ramsey} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is extremely amenable}. \] Each condition implies integral exactness. Finite hom-sets hold because the structures are finite, even when the language is countably infinite.
notes: Known and rechecked: the compact Hausdorff row

statement: Let $G$ be any nonarchimedean topological group and $\Gamma\leq G$ a dense subgroup. For every smooth module $N$, the quotient maps give a natural equality $N_\Gamma=N_G$. If $G$ has an increasing sequence of compact subgroups with dense union, smooth rational coinvariants are exact. Thus Lead 5(a) holds in setting (S).
notes: Proved: dense subgroups and compact averaging

statement: In setting (S), if $V\leq U\leq G$ are open and $[U:V]=m<\infty$, there is an injective morphism of smooth $R[G]$-modules \[ R[G/U]\longrightarrow R[G/V],\qquad [gU]\longmapsto\sum_{uV\in U/V}[guV]. \] It induces multiplication by $m$ on coinvariants. In particular, exactness over $\mathbb F_p$ requires $p\nmid m$. Exactness over all prime fields implies (Fin). If a finite member of the class has an automorphism of order $m>1$, it has no affine equalizer with the identity over any ring in which $m$ is not a unit. Hence integral exactness, quasi-filteredness, and totality each imply (Rig).
notes: Proved: the finite-index obstruction

statement: For a discrete group $H$ and a nonzero unital commutative ring $R$, coinvariants on all $R[H]$-modules are exact if and only if $H$ is locally finite and the order of every finite subgroup is a unit of $R$. For $R=\mathbb Q$ this is local finiteness. For $R=\mathbb Z$ it forces $H=1$.
notes: Proved: the discrete case of Lead 1

statement: Let $M=(\mathbb Z;(d_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z})$, where $d_j(x,y)$ means $y-x=j$, and take all embeddings between finite nonempty induced substructures. This is a countable rigid Fra\"iss\'e class with finite hom-sets and automorphism group $\mathbb Z$ with the discrete topology. Its group is amenable, but its category is not exact over any nonzero ring, is not quasi-filtered, and is not total. Strong amalgamation, (St), and (Op) all fail.
notes: Proved: Lead 6(a)

statement: Let $M=\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Q$, with the equivalence relation of equal first coordinates, the rational order inside each class, and binary relations $d_j$ specifying difference $j$ between first coordinates. Its age with all embeddings satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), and (FA). Its automorphism group is topologically \[ \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb Q,<)^{\mathbb Z}\rtimes\mathbb Z. \] It is amenable. The category has finite hom-sets and fails exactness over every nonzero ring, quasi-filteredness, and totality; (St) and (Op) fail.
notes: Proved: Lead 6(b)

statement: Let $G$ be a nonarchimedean topological group, $H\leq G$ a closed co-precompact subgroup, and $X=\widehat{G/H}$ the completion for the right uniformity. Let $k$ be a commutative ring. Suppose that smooth $k[H]$-coinvariants are exact and that there is a finitely additive, $G$-invariant function \[ \mu:\operatorname{Clop}(X)\longrightarrow k,\qquad \mu(X)=1. \] No positivity or bounded-variation condition is imposed on $\mu$. Then smooth $k[G]$-coinvariants are exact. The same conclusion holds for modules over any unital ring $R$ if $\mu$ is integer-valued and smooth $R[H]$-coinvariants are exact. If $k$ is a field and smooth $k[G]$-coinvariants are exact, such a normalized invariant $k$-valued function exists. Consequently, when $H$ has exact smooth $k$-coinvariants, it is an exact criterion. In particular, an amenable $G$ possessing a co-precompact extremely amenable subgroup has exact smooth rational coinvariants.
notes: Proved: the signed averaging criterion

statement: Let $(P,\prec,<)$ be a finite poset with an independent reference linear order. For a linear extension $\pi=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ of $\prec$, put \[ w_P(\pi)=\sum_{\mathcal B}(-1)^{n+|\mathcal B|}, \] where $\mathcal B$ ranges over the partitions of this list into nonempty consecutive blocks such that every block is a $\prec$-antichain and its elements occur increasingly in $<$. For $P=\varnothing$ the empty partition has weight $1$. These integers are natural under isomorphisms preserving both relations, have total sum $1$, and satisfy, for every induced $Q\subseteq P$ and every linear extension $\tau$ of $Q$, \[ \sum_{\pi|_Q=\tau}w_P(\pi)=w_Q(\tau). \]
notes: Proved: integral weights on finite linear extensions

statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of all finite structures $(P,\prec,<)$, where $\prec$ is a strict partial order and $<$ is an independent linear order, with all induced embeddings as strong embeddings. Its category $A_{\mathcal P}$ satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), and (Op). It is exact over every unital ring, and hence is total. Its automorphism group is not amenable and is therefore not extremely amenable. Consequently rational exactness does not imply amenability, integral exactness with rigidity does not imply extreme amenability, and (CT) does not imply (CC), even in this rigid finite-relational Fra\"iss\'e setting.
notes: Refuted: A.3(i), A.3(iv), and the first clause of A.3(v)

statement: Fix $r\geq2$ and a nonzero finite abelian group $\Lambda$. The cocycle class $\mathcal A_r(\Lambda)$ of R13 satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (St), (Op), (WEI), and (Fin). Its group is amenable. For every commutative unital ring $R$, its colimit functor is exact if and only if $|\Lambda|$ is a unit in $R$. It is not total and does not satisfy (FA$\varnothing$). In particular $\mathcal A_2(\mathbb F_p)$ is rationally exact and satisfies (Fin), but fails exactness over $\mathbb F_p$ and over $\mathbb Z$. Thus absence of finite-index open-subgroup obstructions, even in this rigid setting with (SA), (FA), (St), and (Op), does not make rational exactness imply prime-field or integral exactness.
notes: Refuted: the converses in A.3(vi) and A.3(vii)

statement: Let $A_{E,<}$ be the category of finite sets with an equivalence relation and an independent linear order, with all embeddings. For every prime $p$, this category is not exact over $\mathbb F_p$. More generally, for every integer $m\geq2$ it has an explicit $m$-arrow family without an affine equalizer over any ring in which $m$ is not a unit. In particular, the assertion in A.4(3) that it is exact over all odd prime fields is false.
notes: Refuted: the odd-characteristic clause of FE-1

statement: The group of the independently ordered equivalence structure is amenable but not extremely amenable. Its category is exact over $\mathbb Q$, but not over $\mathbb Z$ or any $\mathbb F_p$, and is neither quasi-filtered nor total. It satisfies (Rig), (SA), (FA), and (FA$\varnothing$), but not (St), (Op), or (Fin).
notes: Proved: rational exactness of the same example

statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a countable abelian group and $r\geq2$. The automorphism group of the strong Fra\"iss\'e limit of $A_r(\Lambda)$ is amenable. Thus $A_2(\Q)$ satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (St), (Op), (WEI), and (Fin), has an amenable automorphism group, and is exact over every prime field, but is not exact over $\Q$ or $\Z$. It is quasi-filtered but is not total, and it does not satisfy (FA$\varnothing$). It has no co-precompact extremely amenable subgroup.
notes: Proved: amenability does not require finite cocycle coefficients

statement: Fix a finite field $k$. Let $\mathcal V_k$ consist of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with zero omitted from the universe, equipped with an arbitrary independent linear order. Include the empty structure for the zero vector space. In the relational language use one relation for each linear equation on nonzero vectors; require the strong embeddings to extend to injective linear maps. Then (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), (Op), (WEI), and (Fin) hold. Its category of nonempty objects is total.
notes: Proved: the structural hypotheses for punctured ordered vector spaces

statement: For every finite field $k$, the automorphism group of the limit of $\mathcal V_k$ in Proposition~\ref{A:ordered-vector-structure} is amenable. Equivalently, its category satisfies (Re) and (CC).
notes: Proved: amenability of independently ordered finite-field vector spaces

statement: Let $\mathcal V^{<}_2$ have as objects the nonzero points of finite positive-dimensional $\mathbb F_2$-vector spaces, with an arbitrary linear order, and as arrows the restrictions of injective linear maps which preserve that order. This category is not exact over $\mathbb F_2$ or over $\mathbb Z$. In fact the five embeddings specified below have no affine equalizer over $\mathbb F_2$ at any target.
notes: Proved: an ordered vector-space parity obstruction

statement: For $k=\mathbb F_2$, the category $\mathcal V_k$ is total and satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), (Op), (WEI), and (Fin). Its group is amenable, but its colimit functor is not exact over $\mathbb F_2$ or over $\mathbb Z$. Thus (CC) together with totality does not imply (CT), even under all the structural hypotheses in A.3(ii). Its group is not extremely amenable.
notes: Refuted: A.3(ii) and the second clause of A.3(v)

statement: The category $C$ of finite nonempty sets with an independent linear order and cyclic order is quasi-filtered, but not total and not exact over any nonzero commutative ring. Its group is neither amenable nor extremely amenable. It satisfies (Rig), (SA), (FA), (St), (Op), and (Fin), but not (FA$\varnothing$). Its classifying space is simply connected and $H_2(BC;\Z)\cong\Z$.
notes: Known and rechecked: the linear--cyclic example R10

statement: The category of nonempty finite graphs with all induced embeddings is exact over $\Q$, but not over $\Z$ or any $\F_p$. It is neither quasi-filtered nor total. Its random graph automorphism group is amenable but not extremely amenable; (St) holds, while (Rig), (Op), and (Fin) fail. It satisfies (SA), (FA), and (FA$\varnothing$).
notes: Proved: finite graphs with all induced embeddings

statement: The entries in the following table hold for the named categories. The column $\F_2$ records exactness over that field. In every row with a negative $\F_2$ entry except where explicitly qualified elsewhere, the proofs above actually give failure in every prime characteristic. \begin{center} \small \begin{tabular}{lcccccccc} \toprule Class & Total & $\Z$ & $\Q$ & $\F_2$ & Amen. & Extr. & St & Op\\ \midrule $\Cdelta$ & yes & no & no & no & no & no & yes & yes\\ Convex equivalence and order & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes & no & no\\ Independent equivalence and order & no & no & yes & no & yes & no & no & no\\ Independent poset and order & yes & yes & yes & yes & no & no & yes & yes\\ Independent cyclic and linear order & no & no & no & no & no & no & yes & yes\\ Finite graphs & no & no & yes & no & yes & no & yes & no\\ $C(2,2,1)$ & yes & no & no & no & no & no & yes & yes\\ $C(3,3,1)$ & yes & no & no & no & no & no & yes & yes\\ Translation structure on $\Z$ & no & no & no & no & yes & no & no & no\\ Fibred translation structure & no & no & no & no & yes & no & no & no\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} None of these categories is filtered.
notes: Proved: the complete table requested in A.4

statement: In setting (S), suppose that $G$ is amenable and its universal minimal flow is metrizable. Then $A$ is exact over $\Q$. Consequently any counterexample to A.3(iii) must have nonmetrizable universal minimal flow. This conclusion does not require (Rig), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), or (Op).
notes: Proved: amenability with metrizable universal minimal flow

statement: Let $A$ and $A'$ be two presentations satisfying (S), with limits $M,N$, and identify their automorphism groups by a topological isomorphism $G$. Suppose $A$ is total. Suppose also that every nonempty finite subset of $N$ has a least finite strong superset, written $\operatorname{cl}_N(S)$. Then $A'$ is total. In particular, totality is a group invariant among presentations whose nonempty intersections of finite strong subsets are strong. No rigidity, functorial amalgamation, or intersection assumption is imposed on the source presentation.
notes: Proved: totality transfers to a presentation with finite closures

statement: Let $A$ be a nonempty connected small category satisfying condition I. Let $C\subseteq A$ be a full subcategory such that every object of $A$ has a morphism to an object of $C$. Then $A$ is total if and only if $C$ is total. Mere objectwise cofinality is sufficient here; homotopy finality is a conclusion, not an additional assumption.
notes: Proved: totality and full cofinal subcategories

statement: In setting (S), totality of the strong embedding category depends only on the topological isomorphism type of $G=\Aut(M)$. Together with Theorem~\ref{A:coinvariants}, this answers both questions in A.1 affirmatively. Neither assertion needs (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), (Op), or an intersection hypothesis.
notes: Proved: unrestricted group invariance of totality

statement: Let $G,H$ be automorphism groups of presentations satisfying (S). If $\rho:G\to H$ is a continuous homomorphism with dense image and a presentation of $G$ is total, then every presentation of $H$ is total. In particular, none of the automorphism groups of the cocycle limits for $\mathcal A_r(\Lambda)$, $r\ge2$, $\Lambda\ne0$, can be a continuous quotient, or a dense continuous image, of a group with a total presentation.
notes: Proved: totality passes to dense continuous images

statement: There is a diagram $M:\mathcal V^{<}_2\to\Ab$ whose values are finite-rank free abelian groups and whose colimit contains an element of order exactly two. This assertion remains valid whether the empty punctured zero-dimensional vector space is included or omitted.
notes: Proved: an integral free-valued diagram with torsion colimit

statement: Let $G$ be the automorphism group of a presentation satisfying \textup{(S)}. If that presentation is total, every \textup{(S)} presentation of every open subgroup $H\leq G$ is total. For any fixed unital coefficient ring $R$, exactness likewise passes from $G$ to an open subgroup, and from $G$ along a continuous homomorphism with dense image to another group having an \textup{(S)} presentation. Consequently no open subgroup of a group with a total presentation can have a nontrivial cocycle group $\operatorname{Aut}(M_{\mathcal A_r(\Lambda)})$, $r\geq2$, $\Lambda\ne0$, as a continuous dense image.
notes: Proved: open subgroups and dense images

statement: Assume (S), and suppose that $G$ is amenable but $A$ is not exact over $\Q$. There is a finite parallel family $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$, with $k\geq1$, for which the following holds. Put $X_b=\operatorname{Emb}_{\leq}(b,M)$ and define the smooth $G$-module homomorphism \[ D:\Q[X_q]\longrightarrow \Q[X_p]^k, \qquad [g]\longmapsto([ga_i]-[ga_0])_{i=1}^k. \tag{DG.1} \] Let $J=\operatorname{im}D$, give the target its sum of the coefficient $\ell^1$ norms, and define on $J$ the quotient seminorm \[ \|w\|_D=\inf\{\|t\|_1:t\in\Q[X_q],\ Dt=w\}. \tag{DG.2} \] Then $J$ is generated by one $G$-orbit. There is a well-defined $G$-invariant $\Q$-linear functional $\lambda:J\to\Q$ with $\lambda(Dt)=\operatorname{aug}t$, and a sequence $w_n\in J$ such that \[ \lambda(w_n)=1,\qquad \|w_n\|_D=1, \qquad \|w_n\|_1\longrightarrow0. \tag{DG.3} \] In particular no constant $C$ satisfies $\|w\|_D\leq C\|w\|_1$ on this submodule. Conversely, if every finite-family image (DG.1) has such a linear filling bound, amenability implies rational exactness.
notes: Proved: the necessary failure of a linear filling bound

statement: Let $\mathcal C$ have as objects finite positive-dimensional $\mathbf F_2$-vector spaces $W$, a distinguished linearly ordered basis $E_W$, and an independent linear order on $W\setminus\{0\}$. Its arrows are injective linear maps taking basis elements to basis elements and preserving both orders. Then $\mathcal C$ is Ramsey, has finite hom-sets and common successors, and is exact over every ring.
notes: Proved: Ramsey property with a distinguished ordered basis

statement: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ be a functor, where $\mathcal C$ is nonempty, has common successors, and is exact over a commutative ring $R$. For $Y\in\mathcal A$ define \[ X_Y(C)=R[\mathcal A(Y,uC)]. \] For a finite family $a_0,\ldots,a_k:P\to Q$, suppose there is $\mu\in\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal C}X_Q$ of augmentation one whose images under every precomposition map $a_i^*:\operatorname{colim}X_Q\to\operatorname{colim}X_P$ agree. Then the family has an affine equalizer over $R$ in $\mathcal A$.
notes: Proved: finite averaging through an exact category

statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of finite nonzero $\mathbf F_2$-vector spaces with an arbitrary linear order on their nonzero vectors and all order-preserving linear embeddings. Then $\mathcal A$ is exact over $\Q$. Consequently the example of Theorem~\ref{A:ordered-vector-counterexample} is total, amenable, and rationally exact, while it is not exact over $\mathbf F_2$ or over $\Z$.
notes: Proved: rational exactness of the ordered-vector example

statement: Assume (S) and (FA). For every covariant action $L:A_M\to\mathrm{Set}$ there are natural transformations \[ L\longrightarrow L^{\mathrm{inj}}\longrightarrow T_S, \qquad S=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal I_M}L^{\mathrm{inj}}, \qquad T_S(B)=S^{G_B}, \] each inducing a weak equivalence on categories of elements. The $G$-set $S$ is smooth. Its orbits are in bijection with the connected components of $\operatorname{El}(T_S)$. For every open $U\leq G$, \[ \operatorname{El}_{A_M}(T_{G/U})\simeq E_U \] as categories, where $E_U$ is the category in Lead 7. Thus $A$ is total if and only if every $BE_U$ is weakly contractible; and $A\in\mathcal Q_n$ if and only if every $BE_U$ is $(n-1)$-connected. Neither implication uses (FA$\varnothing$).
notes: Proved: the general saturation theorem

statement: Let $M$ be either the generic independently ordered equivalence structure or the generic convexly ordered equivalence structure. Write $J=M/E$. A finite closed support in the two-sorted structure $(M,J,\pi)$ is a pair $(P,D)$, where $P\subset M$ and $D\subset J$ are finite and $\pi(P)\subseteq D$. Write $G_{P,D}$ for the subgroup fixing all points of $P$ and all classes of $D$. Then \[ \langle G_{P,D},G_{P',D'}\rangle =G_{P\cap P',D\cap D'}. \] Every open subgroup $U$ has a unique least such finite support $(P,D)$ with $G_{P,D}\leq U$, and is the inverse image of a subgroup of the automorphism group of that finite support under its setwise stabilizer. In the convex case this finite automorphism group is trivial. In the independent-order case it permutes only $D\setminus\pi(P)$, and is the full symmetric group there.
notes: Proved: finite supports after adding the class sort

statement: For convexly ordered equivalence structures every open subgroup is $G_{P,D}$ for a finite pair as in Lemma~\ref{B:equivalence-supports}, and every $BE_U$ is contractible. In the independently ordered case, every open subgroup is determined by such a pair and a subgroup $H\leq\operatorname{Sym}(D\setminus\pi(P))$, and \[ BE_U\simeq BH. \] In particular a single-class stabilizer gives a contractible component in either case, while the stabilizer of an unordered pair of classes in the independent-order case gives $BC_2\simeq\mathbb{RP}^{\infty}$. More generally $BS_m$ occurs for every $m$. The convex category is total, exact over every coefficient ring, and Ramsey; its group is extremely amenable. Nevertheless (Op) and (St) fail in that presentation.
notes: Proved: all open-subgroup component types in A.4(2),(3)

statement: Let $C$ be the class of finite nonempty sets with an independent linear and cyclic order. Its limit satisfies (St) and (Op), and $\operatorname{Fix}(G_B)=B$ for every finite $B$. Every open subgroup is uniquely $G_F$ for a finite set $F$. Under (FA), every $E_U$ is contractible except possibly $E_G=C$, whose classifying space has the nonzero second homology of R10. The group is not amenable and is not extremely amenable.
notes: Proved: (St) and (Op) for the class of R10

statement: As literally stated for all strong classes in (S), B.4 is false: the truncated linear-order example in Proposition~\ref{B:intersection} is the free ordered expansion of the strong class of sets of size zero or at least two. It has (St) but fails (Op). For the usual all-substructure free-amalgamation classes, intersection closure is automatic. The exact additional finite condition used by the alternating argument is the following bridge condition: for each two finite strong supports $B,C$ with intersection $D$, the bipartite graph of their strong copies over $D$, whose edges are strong copies of their joint structure, is connected. This condition is equivalent to (St), since that graph is the coset graph $G_D/G_B\sqcup G_D/G_C$. One sufficient combinatorial way to verify it is closure under the finite alternating cyclic amalgams used in T A.30, with the two distinguished supports embedded strongly and with an order extending their prescribed finite order patterns. For ordinary relational free amalgamation this closure is proved in Proposition~\ref{B:relational-bridge} below. For a general strong class, free amalgamation along a tree does not by itself assert that identifying the ends of that tree leaves an admissible strong structure. The predimension positivity estimate in Part D is precisely the missing verification in that application.
notes: Proved: scope of the free-amalgamation question

statement: Under (S), without (FA), every open $U\leq G$ satisfies \[ \pi_1(BE_U)\cong U\big/\langle G_B:B\text{ finite nonempty strong},\ G_B\leq U\rangle. \] The subgroup in the denominator is normal in $U$. Consequently totality of $A$ implies that each open subgroup is generated by the finite strong pointwise stabilizers which it contains.
notes: Proved: the fundamental group of an orbit component

statement: Under (S), (FA), and (Op), every action component is weakly contractible or weakly equivalent to $BA$. Therefore $A$ is total if and only if $BA$ is weakly contractible, and $A\in\mathcal Q_n$ if and only if $BA$ is $(n-1)$-connected. Adding (FA$\varnothing$) implies totality. No separate rigidity hypothesis is required for this theorem.
notes: Proved: the exact generalization of T A.33

statement: Assume (S) and (FA), and let $F$ be a \emph{nonempty} finite strong set with $G_F\triangleleft U$ of finite index. Then \[ BE_U\simeq B(U/G_F). \] If $F=\varnothing$, the conclusion must instead be $BE_G\simeq BA$. Thus the finite-extension assertion of Lead 7 is false as written when it includes the empty support and assumes only (FA).
notes: Proved, with a necessary exception to Lead 7

statement: Under (S), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), and (WEI), quasi-filteredness, totality, and (Op) are equivalent. Without (FA$\varnothing$), this three-way equivalence is false: $A_2(\mathbb F_2)$ is quasi-filtered, satisfies (FA), (WEI), and (Op), and is not total.
notes: Proved: the WEI criterion and its empty-base scope

statement: Assume (S) and (SA), let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathcal P$ be the conjugacy-invariant collection of subgroups $G_B$ for nonempty finite strong $B$. Let $\mathcal O_{\mathcal P}$ be the full category of smooth transitive $G$-sets $G/G_B$ and $G$-equivariant maps. Then \[ A^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathcal P}. \] Thus a covariant $R$-module diagram on $A$ is a contravariant (right) $\mathcal O_{\mathcal P}$-module. With $\underline R$ denoting the constant \emph{covariant} (left) module, \[ \operatorname{colim}_A V \cong V\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal P}}\underline R,\qquad T_i(V)\cong \operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{\mathcal P}}_i (V,\underline R). \] Exactness is flatness of this constant left module. This is an orbit-category homology statement, but it is not, without changing variance and checking the collection, the usual Bredon homological-dimension-zero assertion about the constant right module. There is a contractible simplicial $G$-space $X_A$, with open isotropy groups from $\mathcal P$, whose orbit space is naturally $B(A^{\mathrm{op}})$, hence homeomorphic to $BA$. Its $H$-fixed space is the nerve of the category of finite strong embeddings whose image is fixed pointwise by $H$. It is a classifying space for a subgroup family only when the corresponding fixed spaces are contractible for every member of that family; this extra condition is not supplied merely by specifying a collection.
notes: Proved with corrections: Lead 12

statement: In setting (S), for each open $U\leq G$ form a category $\mathcal D_U$ with objects $(B,e)$, where $B$ is an object of $E_U$ and $e:B\to M$ is the restriction of an element of $U$. An arrow $(C,e_C)\to(B,e_B)$ is an $E_U$-arrow $f:B\to C$ with $e_Cf=e_B$. Then $\mathcal D_U$ is contractible, $U$ acts on it simplicially by postcomposition, and \[ BE_U\ \cong\ |N\mathcal D_U|/U \] after the canonical reversal of nerve coordinates. Its isotropy groups are exactly the pointwise stabilizers occurring at the finite images. This gives a model in every homotopy degree, including for subgroups not finite extensions of pointwise stabilizers. Under (SA) and (Rig), the images identify $\mathcal D_U$ equivariantly, up to equivalence, with the opposite of the poset of finite strong subsets $B$ with $G_B\leq U$. That poset is identified with $\{V\in\mathcal P:V\leq U\}$ ordered by reverse subgroup inclusion, with $U$ acting by conjugation.
notes: Proved: an explicit model for every $E_U$

statement: In setting (S), if $A$ is total, no open subgroup $U\leq G$ has a proper open normal subgroup. In particular (Fin) holds. This conclusion requires neither (FA) nor (SA).
notes: Proved: a stronger necessary group condition

statement: For countable abelian $\Lambda$ and $r\geq2$, the class of finite ordered $\Lambda$-valued $r$-cocycles, with all induced embeddings, satisfies (S), (Rig), (SA), (FA), (St), and (Op). Every action component is weakly contractible or its projection to $A_r(\Lambda)$ is a weak equivalence, and \[ BA_r(\Lambda)\simeq K(\Lambda,r). \] Consequently $A_n(\mathbb F_2)\in\mathcal Q_n\setminus\mathcal Q_{n+1}$ for every $n\geq2$. For its group, $U=G$ is an open subgroup for which $E_U$ is $(n-1)$-connected but not $n$-connected. The parameter condition $r\geq2$ is essential to the stabilizer proof.
notes: Known and rechecked: DF A.4--A.8

statement: The assertion ``(Rig) and (St) imply (Op)'' in setting (S) requires an additional intersection condition. Let (Int) mean that an intersection of finite strong subsets of $M$ is again an admissible finite strong subset, with the empty subset allowed. Under (Int), (Rig), and (St), the assertion is true. Under the literal pointwise-stabilizer reading of (St), it is false without (Int).
notes: Refuted as literally stated; repaired with (Int)

statement: Let $B,C$ be induced subposets of a finite poset $D$, with an independent linear order on all structures, and put $F=B\cap C$. Let $d_0,d_1:D\to E$ be increasing induced-poset embeddings agreeing on $F$. There is a finite independently ordered poset $Z$, an increasing induced embedding $E\to Z$, and increasing induced embeddings $a_0,\ldots,a_{2N}:D\to Z$ with the prescribed endpoints, such that $a_{2j}|_B=a_{2j+1}|_B$ and $a_{2j+1}|_C=a_{2j+2}|_C$.
notes: Proved: finite bridge for induced poset embeddings

statement: The category of finite posets with an independent linear order and all increasing induced-poset embeddings satisfies (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), and (Op). Its category is total by the all-action theorem in Part B.
notes: Proved: (St) and (Op) for the independently ordered generic poset

statement: Let $\mathcal K$ be a hereditary class of finite structures in a relational language, with all induced embeddings, joint embedding, and free amalgamation. Expand each member by every possible independent linear order. The expanded class has (St) and (Op). More precisely, every alternating bridge of Proposition~\ref{B:poset-bridge} exists in this expanded class.
notes: Proved: the ordinary relational free-amalgamation case of B.4

statement: Let $K$ be a nonempty connected small Kan complex and put $A(K)=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}/K$, with every simplex, including degenerate simplices, allowed as an object. Then $BA(K)\simeq |K|$. Every component of every covariant action on $A(K)$ is either weakly contractible or weakly equivalent, over $|K|$, to a connected covering space of $|K|$. Every connected cover occurs. For countable $K$, this is a class in (S), with (Rig), (SA), and (FA). If $K$ is simply connected it also has (St) and (Op). For general countable connected $K$, let $\Gamma=\pi_1|K|$. Its limit automorphism group $\widehat G$ has a continuous open quotient \[ 1\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow\widehat G \xrightarrow{\rho}\Gamma\longrightarrow1, \] where $G$ is the automorphism group of the rich labelled limit for the universal cover $\widetilde K$. Every open subgroup of $\widehat G$ is either $G_F$ for a nonempty finite subset $F$ of that limit, or $\rho^{-1}(H)$ for a subgroup $H\leq\Gamma$. The first kind has contractible $E_U$; the second has $E_U$ weakly equivalent to the connected cover corresponding to $H$. Thus the theorem specifies all higher homotopy groups and their monodromy, including the subgroups that are not finite pointwise stabilizers.
notes: Known and rechecked: DF A.13, including its open subgroups

statement: For each $n\geq2$ there is a rigid class in (S) and an open subgroup $U$ whose $E_U$ is $(n-1)$-connected and not $n$-connected. One may require $U$ not to be a finite pointwise stabilizer. Moreover, for connected Kan $K$, \[ A(K)\in\mathcal Q_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |K|\text{ is }(n-1)\text{-connected}. \]
notes: Proved: every requested connectivity gap occurs

statement: For every small category $A$, every $M:A\to\Ab$, and every integer $i\geq0$, there is a natural isomorphism of abstract abelian groups \[ \lim_{A^{\op}}^{i}M^\vee\ \cong\ \Hom_{\Z}(L_i\colim_A M,\mathbb T). \] For $M:A\to\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ the analogous duality is \[ \lim_{A^{\op}}^{i}\Hom_{\F_p}(M,\F_p) \cong\Hom_{\F_p}(L_i\colim_A M,\F_p), \] where the dual groups carry their profinite vector-space topologies. For a $\Q$-module diagram, the first displayed formula holds with $L_i\colim_A$ computed in $\Q$-modules and with the Pontryagin dual of its underlying additive group. These statements include empty and disconnected $A$.
notes: C.1; Proved: the bar--cobar duality

statement: For every small category $A$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact; \item $\lim_{A^{\op}}$ takes objectwise surjective morphisms of compact Hausdorff abelian diagrams to surjections; \item $\lim^1_{A^{\op}}K=0$ for every compact Hausdorff abelian diagram $K$; \item every compact torsor diagram on $A^{\op}$ has a point in its limit, namely (CT). \end{enumerate} Replacing compact abelian groups by profinite $\F_p$-vector spaces gives exactness over $\F_p$ and $(\mathrm{CT})_p$. Replacing them by Pontryagin duals of discrete $\Q$-vector spaces gives exactness over $\Q$ and $(\mathrm{CT})_{\Q}$.
notes: C.2; Proved: exactness is the compact torsor property

statement: Fix a prime $p$. If $A$ has finite hom-sets, exactness of $\colim_A$ over $\F_p$ is equivalent to the assertion that every torsor diagram under \emph{finite} $\F_p$-vector spaces has nonempty limit. The forward implication holds for every small category. The converse is false without the hom-set hypothesis, even for a nonempty connected category satisfying condition I.
notes: C.3; Proved and Refuted: finite vector torsors

statement: For a nonempty connected category satisfying I, the condition that every contravariant diagram of nonempty finite sets of uniformly bounded cardinality has nonempty limit does not imply quasi-filteredness. It does not imply an integral affine equalizer even for a single pair.
notes: C.4; Refuted: uniformly bounded finite sets characterize quasi-filteredness

statement: For every small category $A$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\lim^1_{A^{\op}}K=0$ for every profinite abelian diagram $K$; \item $\colim_A$ is exact over $\F_p$ for every prime $p$; \item every objectwise torsion diagram $M:A\to\Ab$ has $T_i(M)=0$ for every $i>0$; \item $\lim^i_{A^{\op}}K=0$ for every profinite abelian diagram and every $i>0$. \end{enumerate}
notes: C.5; Proved: the profinite test

statement: Suppose $A$ has common successors. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item For a pair $a_0,a_1$, existence of an affine equalizer over one $\F_p$ at a target $r$ implies existence of a rational affine equalizer at that same target. If the pair has an affine equalizer over every $\F_p$, possibly at different targets, it has an integral affine equalizer. \item For any finite family and a target $r$ with $A(q,r)$ and $A(p,r)$ finite, if a prime-field affine equalizer exists at $r$ but no rational one does, the prime divides the torsion subgroup of $\coker D(r)$. \item If $A$ has a weakly terminal object and is exact over every $\F_p$, it is filtered and hence exact over $\Z$. The same conclusion holds if $A$ is total and has a weakly terminal object. These conclusions do not require finite hom-sets; in particular every total one-object category is filtered. \end{enumerate}
notes: C.6; Proved: pair equalizers and exceptional primes

statement: Assume $A$ has common successors and is exact over $\F_p$ for every prime. Then it is quasi-filtered. For every objectwise torsion-free $M:A\to\Ab$, each $T_i(M)$, $i>0$, is uniquely divisible. For every finite parallel family its augmentation ideal satisfies $I=0$ or $I=\Z$. Consequently rational exactness and integral exactness are equivalent under the all-prime hypothesis. If a family has $I=0$, define the subfunctor \[ S(r)=\{s\in\Q\otimes P(r):D(r)s\in E(r)\}. \] Then augmentation gives isomorphisms \[ \colim_A S\cong\Q,\qquad \colim_A (\coker D)_{\mathrm{tor}}\cong\Q/\Z. \] If hom-sets are finite, the torsion cokernel at each individual target has only finitely many prime divisors. Thus the possible failure is necessarily distributed among unboundedly many targets.
notes: C.7; Proved: the rational-only obstruction

statement: There is a finite category with three objects, finite hom-sets and common successors, and a triple of parallel arrows with an affine equalizer over $\mathbb F_2$ but none over $\mathbb Q$. This assertion concerns the specified family, not exactness of the category over $\mathbb F_2$.
notes: Proved: modular affine solvability need not lift at one target

statement: Let $K$ be a nonempty contractible Kan complex. Then the category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}/K$ has the morphism Ramsey property. Consequently its colimit functor is exact over every unital ring. In particular, choosing a contractible Dold--Kan complex from an acyclic but nonsplit chain complex does not give a total nonexact example in this family.
notes: Proved: the contractible Kan candidate is already exact

statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $V$ be an abelian group on which multiplication by $p$ is bijective, and put $k=\mathbb F_p$. Suppose $\rho_i:V\twoheadrightarrow V_i$ is a finite family of surjective homomorphisms, with each $V_i$ uniquely $p$-divisible. Let $J_i=\ker(k[V]\to k[V_i])$. Then the finite lattice of ideals generated from the $J_i$ by sums and intersections is distributive. Consequently, a family $z_i\in k[V_i]$ lifts to one $z\in k[V]$ if its images agree in $k[V]/(J_i+J_j)$ for every pair $i,j$. The lift is a finite linear combination of elements of $V$. The same statement holds for affine surjections of torsors under these groups: choose any origin in the source torsor, and the induced origins in its quotients.
notes: Proved: finite marginal lifting in a perfect group algebra

statement: Fix $r\geq2$ and a prime $p$. For every finite ordered rational $r$-cocycle object $S$ there is a finitely supported element \[ \mu_S\in\mathbb F_p[\operatorname{Prim}(S)],\qquad \operatorname{Prim}(S)= \{b\in C^{r-1}(\Delta^S;\mathbb Q):db=c_S\}, \] of augmentation one. These elements may be chosen simultaneously so that every induced embedding $T\to S$ pushes $\mu_S$ to $\mu_T$ by restriction of primitives.
notes: Proved: coherent modular weights on rational primitives

statement: For each $r\geq2$, the category $A=\mathcal A_r(\mathbb Q)$ of finite nonempty ordered rational $r$-cocycles is exact over $\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$, but is not exact over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb Z$. It has finite hom-sets and common successors. It lies in setting (S) and satisfies (Rig), (SA), (FA), (St), (Op), (WEI), and (Fin). It is not total, since $BA\simeq K(\mathbb Q,r)$. Consequently the main all-prime implication in C.4 is false, both with and without the finite-hom hypothesis, and remains false in setting (S) with (Rig). Property (P) does not imply totality, even for these nonempty connected finite-hom rigid strong Fra\"iss\'e categories. The version whose index category is assumed total is not decided by this example.
notes: Refuted: all-prime exactness forces rational exactness

statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a countable abelian group and let $r\geq2$. Then \[ \mathcal A_r(\Lambda)\text{ is exact over }\mathbb F_p \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p:\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda\text{ is bijective}, \] and \[ \mathcal A_r(\Lambda)\text{ is exact over }\mathbb Q \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Lambda\text{ is torsion}. \] Thus it is exact over every prime field $\mathbb F_p$ precisely when $\Lambda$ is a rational vector space, and it is integrally exact precisely when $\Lambda=0$. For a nonzero rational vector space these categories give the counterexamples in Theorem~\ref{C4:counterexample}.
notes: Proved: the complete field profile of cocycle classes

statement: For a triangle of cocycle value one, write a primitive as $(x,y,z)=(b_{01},b_{12},b_{02})$, so $x+y-z=1$. For any prime $p$, put weight $+1$ on \[ (1/p,j/p,(j+1-p)/p),\qquad 0\leq j<p, \] and weight $-1$ on \[ (0,j/p,(j-p)/p),\qquad 1\leq j<p. \] This has $2p-1$ distinct atoms and integral augmentation one. Its three marginals are respectively $p[1/p]-(p-1)[0]$, $[0]$, and $[0]$. Modulo $p$ all are $[0]$. This exhibits explicitly how rational denominators create the modular marginal cancellation, while the rational cocycle still has value one. The exact-arithmetic program \texttt{C4\_perfect\_marginal\_certificate.py} checks the formulas for eight primes; the displayed calculation proves them uniformly.
notes: A finite modular primitive distribution

statement: Let $A$ be nonempty with common successors, and fix a finite parallel family $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$. Write \[ D:\mathbb Z[A(q,-)]\longrightarrow \mathbb Z[A(p,-)]^k, \qquad D(t)=(ta_i-ta_0)_{1\leq i\leq k}, \] and let $S$ be the pointwise saturation of $\operatorname{im}D$ in the target. If $S/\operatorname{im}D$ is annihilated by a positive integer $N$, an affine equalizer over $\mathbb F_p$ for any prime $p\nmid N$ implies a rational affine equalizer for this family. Consequently all-prime exactness implies rational exactness whenever these torsion quotients have bounded exponent for every finite family. The bounded-exponent condition holds if each such saturation functor is generated by finitely many elements at finitely many objects; in particular it holds if finite sums of integral representable functors are Noetherian. In setting (S), an alternative sufficient condition is that every finite sum of the smooth permutation modules $\mathbb Z[G/G_P]$ is Noetherian as a $\mathbb Z[G]$-module. No Noetherian hypothesis is asserted for arbitrary oligomorphic groups or for the independently ordered vector-space example.
notes: Proved: a bounded-denominator criterion

statement: For $A=\mathcal A_2(\mathbb Q)$ there is a diagram $C:A\to\Ab$ that is finitely generated at each object and satisfies \[ T_1(C)\cong\mathbb Z, \qquad \lim_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}^{1} C^\vee\cong\mathbb R/\mathbb Z. \] Every profinite abelian diagram on $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ has vanishing first derived limit, while the displayed compact diagram does not. A nonzero element of $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ gives an objectwise nonempty compact torsor diagram with empty inverse limit.
notes: Proved: a compact torsor witnessing the all-prime failure

statement: Let $A=\Cdelta$, $P_X=A(V,X)$, $E_X=A(W,X)$, and let $k=\F_p$. Define $D_X:k[E_X]\to k[P_X]^2$ by \[ D_X[g]=([gv_2]-[gv_1],\ [gv_3]-[gv_1]),\qquad Q=\coker D. \] The following contravariant diagram consists of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces: \[ K(X)=\left\{(s,t)\in k^{P_X}\times k^{P_X}: s(gv_2)-s(gv_1)+t(gv_3)-t(gv_1)=0\ (g\in E_X)\right\}. \] Its transitions are restriction along postcomposition of embeddings. It is $\Hom_k(Q,k)$ and satisfies $\lim^1K\cong k$. Replacing the right-hand side zero in its defining equations by one gives a nonempty torsor $T(X)$ under $K(X)$ at each object, and $\lim T=\varnothing$. Over $\Z$, use the same $D$, $Q$ and equations with values in $\mathbb T$. Then $K=\Hom_{\Z}(Q,\mathbb T)$ and $\lim^1K\cong\mathbb T$. For each nonzero $\theta\in\mathbb T$, the equations with right-hand side $\theta$ give a torsor without a compatible point.
notes: C.8; Proved: the torsor and its nonzero cocycle

statement: For every prime $p$ there are two diagrams $F,F':\Cdelta^{\op}\to\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, finite dimensional at every object, with \[ \dim F(X)=\dim F'(X)\quad\text{for all }X, \qquad \dim\lim^1F=1,\quad \dim\lim^1F'=0. \] More generally, for any small category $A$, any unital ring $R$, and any objectwise injective map \[ D:\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m}R[A(p_j,-)]\longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}R[A(q_i,-)], \] let $B:R^m\to R^n$ be its induced augmentation map. Then \[ T_1(\coker D)=\ker B,\qquad T_i(\coker D)=0\ (i\geq2),\qquad \colim_A\coker D=\coker B. \] Here $B$ is a morphism of left $R$-modules; for a noncommutative $R$ its entries act on a coordinate on the right.
notes: C.9; Refuted: objectwise dimensions determine the first derived limit

statement: Let $G=F(a,b)$, let $c=(ab)^{-1}$, and put $H_0=\langle a\rangle$, $H_1=\langle b\rangle$, $H_\infty=\langle c\rangle$. Define a category $X$ on the objects $0,1,\infty,U$ by \[ X(U,U)=G,\quad X(x,U)=G/H_x\ (x=0,1,\infty),\quad X(x,x)=\{\id_x\}, \] with all other hom-sets empty. Here $G/H_x$ means left cosets $gH_x$, and composition is $h\circ(gH_x)=hgH_x$ and $h\circ g=hg$. This is a skeleton of the homotopy exit-path category of $\mathbb P^1$ stratified by its three punctures and their complement. Its classifying space is homotopy equivalent to $S^2$. Consequently \[ T_1^X(\Delta\Z)=0,\quad T_2^X(\Delta\Z)=\Z, \qquad \lim^1_{X^{\op}}\Delta\mathbb T=0,\quad \lim^2_{X^{\op}}\Delta\mathbb T=\mathbb T. \]
notes: C.10; Proved: the exit index and its constant coefficients

statement: Use the category and composition convention of Theorem~\ref{C:exit}. For each $x$ choose a coset section $s_x:G/H_x\to G$ with $s_x(H_x)=1$. Define the integer $n_x(g,z)$ by \[ s_x(gz)^{-1}g s_x(z)=\gamma_x^{\,n_x(g,z)}, \qquad (\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\gamma_\infty)=(a,b,c). \] For each $\theta\in\mathbb T$ there is a normalized degree-two cocycle $\omega_\theta$ with value $\theta n_\infty(g,z)$ on $\infty\xrightarrow zU\xrightarrow gU$, and value zero on all other nondegenerate two-simplices. The map \[ \mathbb T\longrightarrow\lim^2_{X^{\op}}\Delta\mathbb T, \qquad \theta\longmapsto[\omega_\theta] \] is an isomorphism. There is no single group-theoretic generator of $\mathbb T$; the requested ``generating cocycle'' is therefore properly a family indexed by $\theta$, or the integral generator whose scalar multiples are this family.
notes: C.11; Proved: an explicit degree-two cobar class

statement: The category $X$ is not quasi-filtered and is not exact over any nonzero ring. It satisfies none of (CH), (CC), (CT). For its constant compact coefficients the first nonzero positive derived limit occurs in degree two; for an explicit nonconstant compact abelian diagram it already occurs in degree one.
notes: C.12; Proved: nonconstant coefficients detect degree one

statement: Let $s\geq2$ and let $a_0,\ldots,a_k:P\to Q$ be a finite family in $\mathcal A_s(\mathbb Q)$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the family has an affine equalizer over $\mathbb Q$; \item there are primitives $b_P\in C^{s-1}(\Delta^P;\mathbb Q)$ and $b_Q\in C^{s-1}(\Delta^Q;\mathbb Q)$ of the specified cocycles such that $a_i^*b_Q=b_P$ for every $i$; \item the family has an affine equalizer over $\mathbb Z$. \end{enumerate} Thus rational equalizability for a fixed family is a finite system of rational linear equations on its two given objects. This assertion concerns the coefficient group $\mathbb Q$ of the cocycles; it is not asserted with a finite coefficient group in its place.
notes: Proved: a finite rational primitive criterion

statement: Let $r,s\geq2$ and let $F:\mathcal A_r(\mathbb Q)\to\mathcal A_s(\mathbb Q)$ be any functor. If $a_0,\ldots,a_k:P\to Q$ is a finite parallel family and $s\geq |Q|$, the family $F(a_0),\ldots,F(a_k)$ has an integral affine equalizer. In particular, for any sequence of functors \[ \mathcal A_{r_0}(\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow \mathcal A_{r_1}(\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow\cdots, \qquad r_n\longrightarrow\infty, \] its filtered colimit as a small category is integrally exact. Consequently this construction cannot give a total all-prime-exact category which fails rational exactness, regardless of the chosen transition functors.
notes: Proved: increasing cocycle degrees erase fixed families

statement: \label{C4:vector-cocycle-colimits} Let $I$ be a nonempty small filtered category. For each $i\in I$, let $V_i$ be a countable rational vector space and let $r_i\geq2$. Allow arbitrary functors in a diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal A_{r_i}(V_i)$, without requiring that they come from linear maps of the coefficient spaces. For its categorical colimit $A$, one has \[ \widetilde H_*(BA;\mathbb Q)=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ is exact over }\mathbb Z. \] Thus every total, or merely weakly contractible-base, colimit of this form is integrally exact, including when the coefficient vector spaces have unbounded or infinite dimension.
notes: Proved: rational-vector coefficient cocycle colimits

statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty small filtered category, let $K_i$ be nonempty connected small Kan complexes, and let \[ A_i=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}/K_i\quad(i\in I) \] form a diagram of categories with arbitrary transition functors. The transition functors need not be faithful or induced by simplicial maps. Put $A=\colim_{i\in I}A_i$, the colimit in small categories. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \[ BA\simeq *;\qquad A\text{ is total};\qquad \colim_A\text{ is exact over }\Z. \] When these conditions hold, $\colim_A$ is exact over every unital ring. Consequently no total counterexample to C.4, and no total nonexact category, can be obtained as such a filtered colimit. This includes arbitrary coefficient groups and arbitrary connected Kan stages; it imposes no increasing-connectivity condition on the stages.
notes: Proved: contractible filtered Kan totalizations are exact

statement: Let $B$ be a nonempty connected small category that is exact over $\mathbb Z$, let $\Lambda:B\to\Ab$ be a diagram of small abelian groups, and fix $r\geq2$. Form the covariant Grothendieck construction \[ A=\int_{b\in B}\mathcal A_r(\Lambda(b)), \tag{GA.1} \] using the coefficient-pushforward functors associated with the homomorphisms of $\Lambda$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\Lambda$ is locally zero: every $v\in \Lambda(b)$ is killed by some arrow out of $b$; \item $A$ is exact over $\mathbb Z$; \item $A$ is total. \end{enumerate} If every $\Lambda(b)$ is uniquely $p$-divisible, then $A$ is exact over $\mathbb F_p$. In particular, rational-vector coefficient assemblies are exact over every prime field, but they give no total counterexample to the all-prime implication.
notes: Proved: cocycle assemblies over an exact base

statement: Let $B$ be a nonempty connected small category exact over $\mathbb Z$. Let $b\mapsto C_b=A(K_b)=\Delta_{\rm inj}/K_b$ be a diagram of categories and arbitrary functors, where every $K_b$ is a nonempty connected small Kan complex. Put $A=\int_B C_b$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $A$ is total; \item $A$ is exact over $\mathbb Z$; \item every positive homology diagram $b\mapsto H_q(BC_b;\mathbb Z)$ is locally zero, and every loop in every $BC_b$ becomes trivial after some base arrow. \end{enumerate} In the last condition, a base arrow acts by the specified transition functor; the target basepoint is its image of the given basepoint. In particular, allowing arbitrary nonfiltered exact bases and arbitrary transition functors still produces no total nonexact category by such an assembly.
notes: Proved: Kan assemblies over an exact base

statement: For every integer $r\geq2$ there are finite objects $P_r,Q_r$ of $\mathcal A_r(\mathbb Q)$ and three increasing embeddings $f_0,f_1,f_2:P_r\to Q_r$ which have no rational affine equalizer. Moreover, their finite simplicial coequalizer \[ R_r=\Delta^{Q_r}/(f_0\Delta^{P_r}=f_1\Delta^{P_r} =f_2\Delta^{P_r}) \] has nonzero rational homology in degree $r$. Thus there is no bound, depending only on the number of arrows, on the homology degree of such finite coequalizers or of their compatible-primitive obstructions. The assertion uses three arrows independently of $r$; the sizes of the two finite objects are allowed to grow with $r$.
notes: Proved: three-arrow obstructions in every cocycle degree

statement: Let $\mathcal U$ be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$. For arbitrary integers $r_i\geq2$, the ordinary category ultraproduct \[ \mathcal C=\prod_{i\to\mathcal U}\mathcal A_{r_i}(\mathbb Q) \] is not exact over any nonzero unital ring and is not total. The same is true of the ultrapower $\prod_{i\to\mathcal U}\Delta_{\rm inj}$, although $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ itself is integrally exact and total. Thus there is no bound on the support size of affine equalizers in terms of the number of parallel arrows alone, even for two arrows in $\Delta_{\rm inj}$.
notes: Proved: ordinary ultraproducts lose modular exactness

statement: In $\Cdelta$, let $V$ be the singleton and let $Q$ have ordered vertices $a<b<c<x<y$ and edges $\{a,x,y\}$ and $\{b,c,y\}$. Consider the three strong arrows $V\to Q$ selecting $a,b,c$. There is a strong target $R$ with $24$ vertices and $14$ edges such that this family has an affine equalizer over $\mathbb F_2$ in $R$, but none over $\Q$ in $R$. Nevertheless the same family has an integral affine equalizer at a larger target in $\Cdelta$.
notes: Proved: targetwise separation need not persist

statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty finite ordered set and let $\sigma,\tau$ be permutations of $I$. For $A\in\Cdelta$, define $F_{I,\sigma,\tau}(A)$ on the lexicographically ordered set $A\times I$ by replacing each increasing edge $a<b<c$ by \[ \bigl\{(a,i),(b,\sigma(i)),(c,\tau(i))\bigr\},\qquad i\in I. \tag{COV.1} \] On arrows put $F(f)(v,i)=(f(v),i)$. This is a strong endofunctor of $\Cdelta$. There is one fixed three-arrow family in $\Cdelta$ whose image under every such functor, and under every finite composition of such functors, has no affine equalizer over any nonzero unital ring. Consequently a filtered colimit of copies of $\Cdelta$ with these transition functors remains nonexact over every nonzero unital ring, although it is total.
notes: Proved: a persistent obstruction for edge covers

statement: For every $(k,a,b)$ the class is a strong amalgamation class with countably many isomorphism types. It satisfies (Rig), (SA), (FA) and (FA$\varnothing$). Intersections of finite strong subsets are strong, and restriction and composition preserve strong embeddings.
notes: Proved: closure calculus and functorial amalgamation

statement: For every $(k,a,b)$, the limit $M$ satisfies (St) and (Op), and $\mathcal C(k,a,b)$ is total. Consequently it is quasi-filtered.
notes: Proved: totality and open stabilizers for all parameters

statement: If $b<(k-1)a$, there is a finite ordered hypergraph $W$ on $n\geq3$ vertices such that \[ a<d:=\delta(W)\leq an/2, \qquad \delta(U)\geq d\quad(2\leq |U|<n). \tag{D1}\label{eq:D-atom} \] In particular $W$ is positive, every singleton is strong in $W$, and its only proper nonempty strong subsets are singletons.
notes: Proved: a finite atom for every nontrivial sparse range

statement: For $b<(k-1)a$ and every nonzero unital ring $R$, $\mathcal C(k,a,b)$ is not exact over $R$. More precisely, for the $W$ of Lemma~\ref{D:atom}, its singleton maps $v_1,\ldots,v_n:V\to W$ have no affine equalizer over $R$. Writing $P_T^R=R[\mathcal C(k,a,b)(T,-)]$, the natural map \[ D_W:P_W^R\longrightarrow(P_V^R)^{n-1},\qquad [g]\longmapsto([gv_i]-[gv_1])_{i=2}^n \tag{D2}\label{eq:D-column} \] is objectwise injective and $T_1(\operatorname{coker}D_W)\cong R$.
notes: Proved: an all-ring obstruction throughout the sparse range

statement: If $b\geq(k-1)a$, then $\mathcal C(k,a,b)$ is Ramsey, is exact over every unital ring, and its ordered limit has extremely amenable automorphism group. If $b\geq ka$, this category is precisely the category of nonempty finite linear orders and increasing injections.
notes: Proved: the complementary range is Ramsey and exact

statement: The group $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ for the ordered class $\mathcal C(k,a,b)$ is amenable if and only if it is extremely amenable, if and only if $b\geq(k-1)a$. The same construction below proves non-amenability for the unordered limit when $b<(k-1)a$.
notes: Proved: amenability classification

statement: For $\mathcal C_\delta$, the graph joining vertices of a common hyperedge is $2$-sparse, and the two stabilizer orbits required by EHN Theorem~3.8 are infinite. More generally its $k$-uniform analogue is sparse when $b>a(k-2)$. If $b\leq a(k-2)$, there is no uniform sparsity bound for the shadow graphs. In particular EHN Remark~3.2, as written, is false for arbitrary sparse relations.
notes: Proved and Refuted: the shadow-graph issue

statement: If $b<(k-1)a$, the ordered limit $M$ has no co-precompact extremely amenable subgroup. Consequently it has no precompact reasonable strong Ramsey expansion whose Fra\"isse limit is an expansion of $M$ in the sense defined in EHN immediately after Remarks~2.19. Orientation expansions with closures must not be described as precompact over this original limit merely because each finite object has finitely many orientations.
notes: Proved: no precompact Ramsey expansion in the negative range

statement: For every prime $p$, the following table gives all parameters. Every category in the table satisfies (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), and (Op). \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccccc} \text{range}&\text{filtered}&\text{exact }\mathbb Z& \text{exact }\mathbb Q&\text{exact }\mathbb F_p& \text{total}&\text{Ramsey}&G\text{ amenable}\\ \hline b<(k-1)a&\text{no}&\text{no}&\text{no}&\text{no}& \text{yes}&\text{no}&\text{no}\\ b\geq(k-1)a&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{yes}& \text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{yes} \end{array} \] In both rows quasi-filteredness holds. Extreme amenability agrees with amenability. No member of this family refutes A.3(i) or A.3(iv). In particular $\mathcal C(2,2,1)$ and $\mathcal C(3,3,1)$ are total, not exact over any nonzero ring, and have non-amenable automorphism groups.
notes: Proved: the complete parameter table

statement: Lead~8(e)'s displayed integral affine equalizer is correct whenever $a>2b$. Its five-edge target is positive exactly when $a>b$, and all its displayed hyperedges are strong exactly when $a>2b$. This equalization of the initial triple does not imply exactness.
notes: Proved: the five-edge certificate and its limits

statement: In the unordered class, the three singleton embeddings into one hyperedge have the rational affine equalizer $\frac16\sum_{\sigma\in S_3}[\sigma]$. Nevertheless its category is not exact over any nonzero ring, including $\mathbb Q$.
notes: Proved: the unordered class of $\mathcal C_\delta$ is not exact

statement: Suppose $u:A^*\to\mathcal C_\delta$ is any Ramsey expansion category with finite hom-sets and common successors, and let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring. Then $\operatorname{colim}_{A^*}$ is exact and $u$ is not homotopy final. The proposed description of $T_1(Q_R)$ as the image of first comma homology under the stated spectral sequence is false: every term $E^2_{1,0}$ of that spectral sequence is zero, so it cannot be $T_1(Q_R)\cong R$.
notes: Proved and Refuted: the expansion spectral sequence

statement: For every small inverse index and every such $d$, there is a natural isomorphism \[ \frac{\lim I}{\im d_\infty} \ \cong\ \ker\bigl(\lim{}^1K\longrightarrow\lim{}^1X\bigr). \] The class of a levelwise solution $y$ is zero if and only if $d_\infty x=y$ has a solution. In general there is no natural map from \emph{all} of $\lim^1K$ into $\coker d_\infty$; the displayed kernel is the subgroup that canonically embeds in that cokernel. For a tower $X_0\leftarrow X_1\leftarrow\cdots$, suppose either \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item all transition maps of $X$ are surjective, with no completeness or metrizability requirement; or \item the $X_n$ are complete metrizable groups and all transition maps have dense image. \end{enumerate} Then \[ \overline{\im d_\infty}=\lim_n\overline{I_n} \quad\text{inside }\lim_nY_n. \] In particular every levelwise solvable $y$ lies in $\overline{\im d_\infty}$. In case (a), $\lim^1X=0$, so the whole group $\lim^1K$ identifies with $\lim I/\im d_\infty$. This is the full closure quotient if every $I_n$ is closed. In general the precise additional quotient is \[ 0\longrightarrow \frac{\lim I}{\im d_\infty} \longrightarrow \frac{\overline{\im d_\infty}}{\im d_\infty} \longrightarrow \frac{\lim\overline I}{\lim I}\longrightarrow0. \] The corresponding assertions hold on every directed set with a countable cofinal subset.
notes: E.1; Proved: the obstruction subgroup and the closure

statement: Even a one-object tower with identity transitions need not identify $\lim^1K$ with the closure quotient if the images $I_n$ are not closed. Take every $X_n=\Z$ discrete, every $Y_n=\mathbb T$, and $d_n(m)=m\alpha\bmod\Z$ for an irrational $\alpha$. Then $K_n=0$, so $\lim^1K=0$, whereas \[ \overline{\im d_\infty}/\im d_\infty =\mathbb T/(\alpha\Z\bmod\Z)\ne0. \] All levelwise solvable compatible elements are already globally solvable. The additional closure classes fail to be levelwise solvable. This is exactly the last quotient in Theorem~\ref{E:obstruction}.
notes: E.2; Proved: why closure and local solvability differ

statement: Let $t$ be a positive transcendental real number. For each $n\geq1$ let \[ X_n=\operatorname{span}_{\Q}\{(t^j,1):j\geq n\}\subset\R^2, \qquad Y_n=\Q\subset\R, \] with their subspace topologies. Use inclusions $X_{n+1}\hookrightarrow X_n$, identity transitions on $Y$, and the second-coordinate map $d_n:X_n\to\Q$. Every inclusion has dense image, because two distinct displayed vectors have a $\Q$-span dense in $\R^2$. Every $d_n$ is continuous and surjective. However $\bigcap_nX_n=0$: transcendence makes the family $(t^j,1)$ linearly independent over $\Q$, and a vector belonging to every tail span has empty finite support. Thus $\lim X=0$, while $1\in\lim Y=\Q$ is levelwise solvable and is outside the closure of the zero image. The groups $X_n$ are not complete. This refutes the version with only dense transitions and no completeness assumption.
notes: E.3; Proved: dense transitions need completeness

statement: For a small category $A$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item every levelwise solvable element for every morphism of compact Hausdorff abelian $A^{\op}$-diagrams is globally solvable; \item $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact. \end{enumerate} For every such compact morphism, $\im d_\infty$ is closed. Consequently any levelwise solvable element that is not globally solvable lies outside the closure of the image. If $A$ is directed, every positive derived limit of every compact Hausdorff abelian diagram vanishes, with no countability assumption and no assumption on the transition maps.
notes: E.4; Proved: the compact regime

statement: There is an inverse system of complete metrizable abelian groups over the directed ordinal $\omega_1$, with surjective transitions, and an objectwise surjective morphism to the constant finite group $\F_2$, for which the source limit is zero. Thus the levelwise solvable element $1$ is outside the closure of the global image, although the index is directed and hence exact.
notes: E.5; Refuted: surjective towers can be replaced by arbitrary directed indices

statement: The two specified model cases have the following operators and obstruction groups. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item On the tower indexed by positive integers, take $X_n=\Z$ with identity transitions, $Y_n=\Z/2^n\Z$ with reduction maps, and $d_n$ reduction. Then $d_\infty:\Z\to\Z_2$ has dense proper image, every finite-level equation is solvable, and \[ \lim{}^1(2^n\Z)\cong\Z_2/\Z. \] \item Over $\Cdelta^{\op}$ take $d_X=D_X^\vee:k^{P_X\,2}\to k^{E_X}$ from Proposition~\ref{C:explicit-torsor}, for $k=\F_p$, and the constant compatible right-hand side one. Every $d_X$ is surjective, but the limit map is the zero map $k^2\to k$. Its cokernel and the kernel-diagram obstruction group are both $k$. In the discrete metric on $k$, the distance of one from the limit image is one. Replacing $k$ by $\mathbb T$ and the right-hand side by $0\ne\theta$ gives the same statements with obstruction group $\mathbb T$; its distance from zero is positive for any fixed compatible metric on $\mathbb T$. \item The system of Theorem~\ref{E:uncountable} has zero levelwise gap and limit gap one in $\F_2$, but its index is exact. Its obstruction belongs to $\ker(\lim^1K\to\lim^1X)$ and contains the injected copy of $\F_2$ supplied by the connecting map. We do not identify all of $\lim^1K$ with $\F_2$. \end{enumerate}
notes: E.6; Proved: the model obstructions and their gaps

statement: Let $I$ be a directed set with a countable cofinal subset, and let $A:I^{\op}\to\Ab$ be a diagram of countable abelian groups. Then $\lim^1_I A$ is zero or uncountable. In particular a nonzero finite $\lim^1$ of a diagram of finite abelian groups cannot occur on a directed index. For arbitrary directed indices the latter assertion also follows from compact duality, since finite groups are compact.
notes: E.7; Known and independently reproved: countable derived-limit dichotomy

statement: Among nonempty connected small categories there are strict inclusions \[ \{\text{filtered}\}\ \subsetneq\ \{\text{exact over }\Z\}\ \subsetneq\ \{\text{total}\}\ \subsetneq\ \{\text{quasi-filtered}\}. \] Successive separating witnesses are $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, $\Cdelta=C(3,2,3)$, and $A_2(\F_2)$. The last witness may be replaced by the repaired Ad\'amek--Koubek--Reiterman category of the supplied TOTAL\_EXACT\_2 return. Thus the conjectured implication from total asphericity to filteredness is false in two successive stronger forms.
notes: Known and rechecked: the statement for II ms.\ 36ter

statement: The requested classes have the following properties. ``Fil'' means filtered, ``Tot'' total, ``Qf'' quasi-filtered, ``Ram'' the morphism Ramsey property, and ``Am'' amenability of the limit automorphism group. The columns $\Z,\Q$ refer to exactness of colimits. All entries are proved; no bounded finite search is used to assert an entry. \begin{center} \small \setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt} \begin{tabular}{lccccccc} \toprule Class & Fil & $\Z$ & $\Q$ & Tot & Qf & Ram & Am\\ \midrule $\Cdelta$ & no & no & no & yes & yes & no & no\\ Convex equivalence and order & no & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes\\ Independent equivalence and order & no & no & yes & no & no & no & yes\\ Independent poset and order & no & yes & yes & yes & yes & no & no\\ Independent cyclic and linear order & no & no & no & no & yes & no & no\\ Finite graphs & no & no & yes & no & no & no & yes\\ $C(2,2,1)$ and $C(3,3,1)$ & no & no & no & yes & yes & no & no\\ Translation structure on $\Z$ & no & no & no & no & no & no & yes\\ Fibred translation structure & no & no & no & no & no & no & yes\\ $C(k,a,b)$, $b<(k-1)a$ & no & no & no & yes & yes & no & no\\ $C(k,a,b)$, $b\geq(k-1)a$ & no & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center}
notes: Proved: the companion classification table

statement: Let $J$ be a nonempty connected small category with exact integral colimits. For every $M:J\to\FreeMon$, the canonical functor \[ q_M:\int_J M\longrightarrow \mathbf B\bigl(\colim_J^{\Mon}M\bigr) \] has a weakly contractible target-under-comma category, and is a weak equivalence. This is DF D.6, with arbitrary ranks and arbitrary unit-preserving substitutions.
notes: Known, rechecked: the exact-index comparison

statement: For $M:A\to\Mon$, put $T_S(B)=S^{G_B}$. The natural monoid map $M\to T_S$ induces a weak equivalence on the homotopy colimits of classifying spaces and an isomorphism on ordinary monoid colimits. For $M:A\to\FreeMon$, every finite subset of $S$ lies in a finite free submonoid. It has a least such free hull. The hull of a finite set fixed pointwise by a subgroup is itself fixed pointwise. Consequently the universal comparison question on $A$ reduces to finite-rank free monoids with injective transitions, as in DF D.8--D.9.
notes: Known, rechecked: saturation and finite free charts

statement: Let $M:A\to\FreeMon$. Suppose that in its smooth filtered-limit monoid $S$ no element is a proper left multiple of another element in its $G$-orbit: \[ x=(g x)w\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w=1 \qquad(x,w\in S, g\in G). \tag{G.1} \] Then $q_M$ is a weak equivalence and $L_i\colim_A(M_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$. In particular failure of either conclusion forces a relation $x=(g x)w$ with $w\ne1$. A strictly positive invariant additive length implies (G.1), but is not needed in this proposition.
notes: Proved: the orbit-divisibility obstruction

statement: If every $M(B)$ has free rank at most one, then $q_M$ is a weak equivalence and $L_i\colim_A M_{\ab}=0$ for $i>0$. Erasing transitions and rank-zero values are allowed.
notes: Proved: rank at most one cannot fail

statement: For $B\in A$, let $M_{\rm gap}(B)$ be the free monoid on the gaps of $\{-\infty\}\cup B\cup\{+\infty\}$, and let an increasing strong embedding send a gap to the product of all intervening gaps. Then its specified comparison $q_{M_{\rm gap}}$ is a weak equivalence. Let $O=G\backslash M_0$ be the set of orbits of \emph{all raw points}. There are natural identifications \[ (M_{\rm gap})_{\ab}\cong\Z[\Und(B)]\oplus\underline\Z, \qquad L_i\colim_A(M_{\rm gap})_{\ab}=0\quad(i>0), \] and both sides of its comparison have type $K(F(O\amalg\{*\}),1)$. In the full category $O$ need not be a singleton; replacing raw points by $A(V,-)$ would be incorrect.
notes: Proved: the specified gap comparison passes

statement: Let $M:A\to\FreeMon$, where $A=\Cdelta$, and put $C=\colim_A^{\Mon}M$. If $C$ has no idempotent other than $1$, then its specified comparison $q_M$ is a weak equivalence and $T_i(M_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$. In particular this holds if $C$ is left cancellative or right cancellative. More precisely, use the smooth locally free $G$-monoid $S$ of Proposition~\ref{G:saturation}, so that $C=S_G$. If $x=(gx)w$ with $w\ne1$, then $C$ contains an idempotent $e\ne1$ such that \[ [x]e=[x],\qquad e[w]=[w]. \tag{G.7} \]
notes: Proved: idempotent-free colimits pass

statement: Let $M:A\to\FreeMon$, where $A=\Cdelta$, and let $S$ be its smooth filtered-limit monoid. If $G$ acts trivially on $S_{\ab}$, then $q_M$ is a weak equivalence and $T_i(M_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$. The same conclusions hold if the smooth rational representation $\Q\otimes S_{\ab}$ is locally finite dimensional, meaning that the linear span of each $G$-orbit is finite dimensional. In particular they hold if $S_{\ab}$ has finite rational rank, and for every diagram whose free ranks have one finite uniform bound. Conversely, any failure of either conclusion forces a proper same-orbit prefix and arbitrarily large linearly independent finite subsets of one $G$-orbit in $\Q\otimes S_{\ab}$.
notes: Proved: bounded ranks pass

statement: Suppose $M:A\to\FreeMon$ has injective transitions, and choose $u,v\in M(V)$. Write $u_i=M(v_i)u$ and $v_i'=M(v_i)v$ in $M(W)$. If \[ u_2v_3'=u_1v_1', \tag{G.9} \] then $u_2=u_1$ and $v_3'=v_1'$. Thus the abelian incidence relator of R3 cannot be lifted by this direct positive two-word equation while retaining its nonzero difference classes. Likewise the alternative proposed lift $u_2=t u_1$, $v_1'=t v_3'$ cannot extend injectively from $V,W$ to $A$ when $t\ne1$. More generally, if only the original group equation $u_2u_1^{-1}v_3'(v_1')^{-1}=1$ is assumed, then the vector $[u_2]-[u_1]$ in $M(W)_{\ab}$ is either zero or has both positive and negative coordinates in its free abelian basis.
notes: Proved: the direct positive incidence lift collapses

statement: Let $\Omega$ be the $G$-orbit of the strong singleton points of $M_0$. A $G$-invariant partial order on $\Omega$ whose principal downsets are linearly ordered is either equality, the given linear order, or its reverse.
notes: Proved: invariant tree orders on strong singletons

statement: Let $M:A\to\FreeMon$ have injective transitions and let $u,v\in M(V)$. Suppose the original DF D.4 group relator holds in $M(W)^{\gp}$: \[ u_2u_1^{-1}v_3'\,(v_1')^{-1}=1. \tag{G.12} \] In the smooth inclusion-colimit monoid $S$, let $u_x,v_x$ be the corresponding elements at $x\in\Omega$. Either both families are constant, or, for any two distinct points $x,y$, the elements $u_x,u_y$ are incomparable both as left and as right factors, as are $v_x,v_y$, and as are $u_x,v_y$. In particular, neither cross-family lift \[ v_3'=u_1t,\quad v_1'=u_2t, \qquad\hbox{or}\qquad u_1=v_3't,\quad u_2=v_1't \tag{G.13} \] can extend injectively to $A$ while keeping the families nonconstant. The same assertion holds with a common left factor instead of the displayed common right factor.
notes: Proved: separated positive incidence families

statement: On the full subcategory of $A$ with objects $V,W$ there is an injective free-monoid diagram whose group completion is the restriction of DF D.4 and whose abelianization is the incidence cokernel of R3. All six point-generator images are a bifix code, and the incidence difference has both a positive and a negative coordinate in the free abelian basis.
notes: Proved: a local rectangle realizes the full free-group diagram

statement: Let $J$ be any total category and let $R$ be a ring. For a diagram $N:J\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ put \[ K(a)=\{x\in N(a):N(f)x=0\text{ for some }f:a\to b\}, \qquad N^{\mathrm{inj}}(a)=N(a)/K(a). \] Then $K$ is a subfunctor, all transition maps of $N^{\mathrm{inj}}$ are injective, and the quotient induces \[ L_i\colim_JN\ \cong\ L_i\colim_JN^{\mathrm{inj}} \qquad(i\ge0). \tag{G.16} \] No finite-hom-set or finite-generation assumption is needed.
notes: Proved: module injectivization preserves derived colimits

statement: Let $J$ be total, let $k$ be any field, and let $N:J\to k\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ satisfy $\dim_kN(a)\le d$ for one finite integer $d$ and every $a$. Then $L_i\colim_JN=0$ for all $i>0$. Moreover the kernel of $N(a)\to\colim_JN$ is exactly $K(a)$ from Proposition~\ref{G:moduleinjectivization}. If instead every $N(a)$ is a finitely generated free abelian group and their ranks have one finite uniform bound, the same acyclicity conclusion holds, and $\colim_JN$ is torsion-free. In particular the abelianization of every uniformly bounded finite-rank free-monoid diagram is acyclic over every total index, even without the Fra\"iss\'e hypotheses of this part.
notes: Proved: bounded dimensions are acyclic on every total index

statement: Let $J$ be any total category and $M:J\to\Mon$. If every canonical map $M(a)\to C=\colim_J^{\Mon}M$ is injective, then the specified canonical comparison $q_M$ is a weak equivalence. Moreover every diagram whose values have free rank at most one passes over every total $J$, including diagrams with erasing transitions.
notes: Proved: injective colimit cocones and all rank-one diagrams

statement: Fix a nonempty $F_0\in\Cdelta$ and any fixed listing of its vertices. Order $L(X)=\Cdelta(F_0,X)$ lexicographically by that listing; the increasing listing is a special case. Let $M_{F_0}(X)$ be the free monoid on the consecutive gaps of $\{-\infty\}\cup L(X)\cup\{+\infty\}$, with a strong embedding acting by subdivision of gaps. The set $L(X)$ may be empty. Then the specified comparison $q_{M_{F_0}}$ is a weak equivalence and $T_i((M_{F_0})_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$. Its target is a $K(F_2,1)$. More precisely, list the distinct strong closures in $F_0$ of the initial segments of the chosen listing as \[ \varnothing=B_0\subsetneq B_1\subsetneq\cdots \subsetneq B_d=F_0. \] The ordinary monoid colimit has presentation \[ P_d=\langle l,r,e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}\mid e_i e_j=e_{\min(i,j)},\quad le_i=l,\quad e_i r=r \ (0\le i,j<d)\rangle. \tag{G.17} \] In particular the strong-hyperedge gap diagram, $F_0=W$, has two distinct nonidentity idempotents $e_0,e_1$ in its ordinary colimit and still passes.
notes: Proved: lexicographic embedding-gap diagrams pass

statement: Let $J$ be any total category, and let $M:J\to\FreeMon$ have free ranks bounded by one finite integer $d$. Put $C=\colim_JM$ in $\Mon$, and let $C_{\ab}$ denote its universal abelian group. Then $C_{\ab}$ is torsion-free of rank at most $d$, and the map $C\to C_{\ab}$ has inverse image of $0$ equal to $\{1\}$. Moreover, the image $P\subseteq C_{\ab}$ satisfies $P\cap(-P)=\{0\}$. In particular $C$ has no nonidentity idempotent or unit, and \[ cx=c\ \text{or}\ xc=c\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=1. \] No Fra\"iss\'e hypothesis is needed.
notes: Proved: bounded rank forbids absorption in the colimit

statement: Call a monoid locally free if every finite subset lies in a finite-rank free submonoid. If $S,T$ are locally free, $X\subset S$ is finite, and $f:S\to T$ is any monoid homomorphism, then \[ f(H_S(X))\subseteq H_T(fX), \] where $H$ denotes the intrinsic least free hull. Erasing and noninjective homomorphisms are allowed. Let $J$ be a small category with finite hom-sets. Every diagram $N:J\to\Mon$ with locally free values is a filtered union of subdiagrams with finite-rank free values. Consequently every free-monoid comparison over $J$ is a weak equivalence if and only if the same holds for all locally free monoid diagrams.
notes: Proved: functorial free hulls and locally free tests

statement: Assume setting (S), and assume its strong embedding category $A$ is total. For a smooth action of $G=\Aut(M_0)$ by automorphisms on a locally free monoid $S$, let $(NS)/G$ be the degreewise orbit simplicial set, with $n$-simplices $S^n/G$. Let $S_G$ be the monoid quotient by the congruence generated by $s=gs$. Then $A\in\mathcal F$ if and only if, for every such $S$, the canonical map \[ \theta_S: |(NS)/G|\longrightarrow B(S_G) \tag{G.19} \] is a weak equivalence. For each $i>0$, the assertion that $L_i\colim_A M_{\ab}=0$ for every $M:A\to\FreeMon$ is equivalent to \[ H_{i+1}(|(NS)/G|;\Z)=0 \quad\text{for every smooth locally free }G\text{-monoid }S. \tag{G.20} \] Consequently both the class-$\mathcal F$ property and these abelianization-acyclicity properties are invariant under changing the total Fra\"iss\'e presentation of the same topological group. Together with Corollary~\ref{A:totality-group-invariant}, membership in $\mathcal F$ depends only on the topological group throughout setting (S), without the extra hypotheses (Rig), (SA), (FA), (FA$\varnothing$), (St), (Op), or (WEI).
notes: Proved: an intrinsic group criterion for the free-monoid test

statement: Let $F\in\Cdelta$ be finite and strong, and put $\Omega_F=\Cdelta(F,M_0)$. Let $\preceq$ be a $G$-invariant partial order on $\Omega_F$ whose principal downsets are chains. Then there are strong subsets and coordinates \[ E=B_0\subsetneq B_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq B_d=F, \qquad a_i\in F\setminus B_{i-1},\quad B_i=\operatorname{cl}_F(B_{i-1}\cup\{a_i\}), \] and signs $\epsilon_i\in\{+1,-1\}$ with the following description. Two distinct embeddings are comparable exactly when they agree on $E$. Within each such fiber their order is lexicographic: at the first $i$ for which their restrictions to $B_i$ differ, compare their values at $a_i$, in the raw order if $\epsilon_i=+1$ and in its reverse if $\epsilon_i=-1$. The equality order corresponds to $E=F$ and $d=0$. The same assertion holds relative to a fixed embedding of any strong $B\subseteq F$, with $G_B$ in place of $G$, and then $B\subseteq E$. In particular every comparability component of such an order is a chain.
notes: Proved: invariant tree orders are finite signed lexicographic orders

statement: Let $S$ be any smooth locally free $G$-monoid for $G=\Aut(M_0)$ of $\Cdelta$. Let $x\mapsto u_x$ and $x\mapsto v_x$ be $G$-equivariant maps from the orbit $\Omega$ of strong singletons to $S$. Suppose that for every strong ordered hyperedge $a<b<c$, \[ u_bu_a^{-1}v_c v_a^{-1}=1\quad\text{in }S^{\gp}. \tag{G.25} \] Then both families are constant. In particular the DF D.4 free-group diagram has no free-monoid lift over all of $\Cdelta$ with these nonconstant point generators, even after allowing arbitrary extra free generators and arbitrary rectangle factorizations at the hyperedges.
notes: Proved: the full incidence group relator has no nonconstant positive realization

statement: For the independently ordered punctured $\mathbb F_2$-vector-space category, let \[ N(B)=\mathbb Z^{\mathcal T(B)} \] be the natural-order function diagram from Proposition~\ref{A:ordered-vector-integral-torsion}, with its point-indicator bases. There is no free-monoid diagram with these specified free bases whose abelianization maps are the pullback maps of $N$.
