The obstruction already occurs on one finite commuting diagram with objects of dimensions one, two, and three. This assertion does not exclude a different choice of bases or a stabilized positive realization of a different diagram.
notes: Proved: the natural-order pullback bases do not lift to words

statement: The positive pattern \[ u_a=pq,\qquad u_b=rq,\qquad v_c=sp,\qquad v_a=sr \tag{G.27} \] has the incidence relation $[u_b]-[u_a]+[v_c]-[v_a]=0$ after abelianization, but its four core words are freely independent in the free group on $p,q,r,s$. There is a free-monoid diagram on the full subcategory of $\Cdelta$ with objects $V,W,X_{11}$ from (G.10), with ranks $2,6,1213$, in which every edge has form (G.27), all transition homomorphisms are injective, the twenty-two point words are pairwise bifix, and their only integral linear relations are the six prescribed incidence relations. Moreover, the six $q$-values form one strict suffix chain and the six $s$-values one strict prefix chain, both ordered by the signed lexicographic flag $(-a,-b)$ on an edge $(a,b,c)$. The existence of an extension to all of $\Cdelta$ is not asserted.
notes: Proved: a twisted finite lift with both global cut chains

statement: Every $G$-invariant partial order on the strong-singleton orbit $\Omega$ is equality, the raw linear order, or its reverse. No assumption on principal downsets is required.
notes: Proved: all invariant orders on strong singletons

statement: Let $S$ be a smooth locally free $G$-monoid, and let $x\mapsto u_x$ and $x\mapsto v_x$ be equivariant maps from $\Omega$ to $S$. Suppose that in $S_{\ab}$ \[ [u_b]-[u_a]+[v_c]-[v_a]=0 \] for every strong ordered edge $(a,b,c)$. Then either both abelianized point families are constant, or both are injective and are antichains for the pointed cone $P=\operatorname{im}(S\to S_{\ab})$. Assume the nonconstant case. If equivariant edge factors $p_e,q_e,r_e,s_e\in S$, for $e=(a,b,c)$, satisfy \[ u_a=p_eq_e,\qquad u_b=r_eq_e,\qquad v_c=s_ep_e,\qquad v_a=s_er_e, \] then each of $q_e,s_e$ has full strong support $e$. Their respective suffix and prefix orders are global linear orders on the edge orbit, and they have exactly the same signed two-coordinate lexicographic flag. Thus only the $24$ identical-flag regimes remain possible, among the $576$ pairs of flags.
notes: Proved: abelian antichains synchronize the twisted cuts

statement: Let $S$ be any locally free monoid, of arbitrary cardinality, and put $K=S^{\gp}$. The map $S\to K$ is injective, $K$ is locally free as a group, and \[ x\le y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^{-1}y\in S \qquad(x,y\in K) \] is a left-invariant partial order with linearly ordered intervals and the interpolation property \[ x_1,x_2\le y_1,y_2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists k\in K\quad x_1,x_2\le k\le y_1,y_2. \] For $E\subseteq K$, write $E^u$ and $E^l$ for its common upper and lower bounds. A bounded Dedekind--MacNeille cut is a pair $c=(D,U)$ satisfying \[ D=U^l\ne\varnothing,\qquad U=D^u\ne\varnothing. \] Its stabilizer $K_c=\{g\in K:gD=D\}$ under left translation maps injectively to $K_{\ab}=S_{\ab}$ and is locally cyclic. If a topological group $G$ acts smoothly on $S$ by monoid automorphisms, its induced action on the cuts obtained from principal cuts by finitely many bounded meets and joins is smooth. For $G=\Aut(M_0)$ of $\Cdelta$, let $\mathscr D$ be any invariant smooth set of bounded cuts. Each cut stabilizer $G_c$ fixes $K_c$ pointwise. Consequently, for every unital ring $R$, including the zero ring, the coefficient diagram \[ N_R(B)=\bigoplus_{c\in\mathscr D^{G_B}} R\otimes_{\Z}K_c \] has $L_i\colim_{\Cdelta}N_R=0$ for every $i>0$. The transition along an embedding extended by $g\in G$ sends the summand at $c$ to the summand at $gc$ by $1\otimes g$. These assertions do not assert that this cut completion is a tree or supplies an acyclic interval resolution.
notes: Proved: bounded cut stabilizers are locally cyclic

statement: Let $S$ be a locally free monoid, $K=S^{\gp}$, and $P=(K,\le)$ the prefix order of Proposition~\ref{G:cutstabilizers}. Inside its bounded Dedekind--MacNeille completion, let $T$ be the closure of the principal cuts under finitely many bounded binary meets and joins. There is a canonical median pretree structure on $T$ whose segment between comparable points is their full order interval. Every segment is a finite concatenation of order intervals, and its turns are obtained by bounded binary meets and joins. The order-preserving actions of $K$ and of every group of monoid automorphisms of $S$ preserve this pretree structure. If the latter action is smooth, its action on $T$ is smooth. Every $K$-point stabilizer in $T$ is locally cyclic. For every subgroup $U$ of the automorphism group, the fixed-point poset $T^U$ has weakly contractible nerve; no openness assumption on $U$ is needed. This supplies a tree of ordered intervals, not a simplicial tree with a permutation module of edges. No equivariant homology resolution or free-monoid comparison follows here by assertion.
notes: Proved: finite-parameter median tree completion

statement: For smooth locally free monoids $S$ of the group $G$ of $\Cdelta$, the canonical homomorphism \[ (S^G)^{\gp}\longrightarrow (S^{\gp})^G \] need be neither injective nor surjective. The two explicit examples below come from finite-rank free-monoid diagrams over $\Cdelta$. Both diagrams satisfy $T_i(M_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$, so these examples do not settle the remaining general $T_1$ or comparison question.
notes: Proved: neither direction of the fixed-group identification

statement: In setting \textup{(S)}, suppose the strong-embedding category is total. Let $G=\Aut(M)$, let $U\leq G$ be open, and let \[ 1\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow E\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}U \longrightarrow1 \] be an extension of topological groups with discrete abelian kernel, where $p$ is a quotient map. Suppose the extension is central. Then it has a unique continuous homomorphic section over $U$. For the group of $\Cdelta$, in particular, a point $c$ of the tree $T$ in Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree} has a stabilizer in $K\rtimes G$ fitting into \[ 1\longrightarrow K_c\longrightarrow (K\rtimes G)_c \longrightarrow G_{Kc}\longrightarrow1, \] and this is canonically a direct product of $K_c$ and a uniquely specified lift of $G_{Kc}$. Here $G_{Kc}$ denotes the setwise stabilizer of the $K$-orbit of $c$, not the point stabilizer $G_c$. Let $\Gamma=K_G$ be the group of coinvariants and let $\rho:K\rtimes G\to\Gamma$ send $(k,g)$ to the class of $k$. The uniquely lifted copy $\widehat{G_{Kc}}$ is killed by $\rho$. Consequently \[ \rho((K\rtimes G)_c)=\rho(K_c),\qquad \ker(\rho)\cap(K\rtimes G)_c =\ker(\rho|K_c)\times\widehat{G_{Kc}}. \] In particular the image stabilizer in $\Gamma$ is locally cyclic. This splitting does not assert that its lifted subgroup is $K$-conjugate to the standard copy of $G_{Kc}$.
notes: Proved: uniqueness and existence of a global central splitting

statement: There is a smooth locally free $G$-monoid $S$, for the group of $\Cdelta$, and a continuous $1$-cocycle $\kappa:G\to S^{\gp}$ whose affine action on the tree of Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree} fixes a cut obtained by one bounded binary join, but fixes no original group vertex. Thus the lifted subgroup in Proposition~\ref{G:centralextensions} need not be conjugate by $S^{\gp}$ to a subgroup of the standard copy of $G$.
notes: Proved: a bounded affine fixed cut without a fixed group vertex

statement: Suppose a topological group $U$ has a total presentation in setting \textup{(S)}. Let $X$ be a nonempty simplicial $U$-set whose action in every degree is smooth. If $X$ is connected and integrally acyclic, then $X/U$ is connected and integrally acyclic. If $X$ is weakly contractible, then $X/U$ is weakly contractible. Here the quotient is the degreewise simplicial quotient followed by realization; no separation assumption on a topological orbit space is being substituted for this construction.
notes: Proved: acyclic smooth spaces over a total group

statement: Let $G$ be the group of $\Cdelta$, let $S$ be a smooth locally free $G$-monoid, and put $K=S^{\gp}$ and $H=K\rtimes G$. Let $P$ be the prefix poset of $K$ and $T$ its tree completion. There is a natural weak equivalence \[ \bigl|(NP\times NT)/H\bigr|\ \longrightarrow\ |(NS)/G|. \tag{TD.1} \] For a simplex $\sigma$ of $NT$, write $H_\sigma$ for its pointwise stabilizer and $A_\sigma=K\cap H_\sigma$. Then $A_\sigma$ is torsion-free locally cyclic and \[ |NP/H_\sigma|\simeq K(A_\sigma,1). \tag{TD.2} \] These fibres are the rows of one explicit bisimplicial set, so all their incidence maps are retained. In particular there is a homology spectral sequence converging to $H_*((NS)/G;\Z)$, with \[ E^1_{n,q}=\bigoplus_{[\sigma]\in (NT_n)/H} H_q(A_\sigma;\Z),\qquad E^1_{n,q}=0\quad(q\geq2). \tag{TD.3} \] The $q=0$ row is the simplicial chain complex of $NT/H$; the $q=1$ row has the indicated stabilizer groups and the face maps induced by inclusions and conjugation. Formula (TD.3) alone does not assert that either horizontal row is acyclic, or that the remaining differential between them vanishes.
notes: Proved: a coherent tree model with locally cyclic fibres

statement: Let $S$ be a locally free monoid and $K=S^{\gp}$. The submonoid $S\subseteq K$ is root-closed: if $z^m\in S$ for $z\in K$ and an integer $m\ge1$, then $z\in S$. Every bounded Dedekind--MacNeille cut stabilizer $K_c$ in Proposition~\ref{G:cutstabilizers} is likewise root-closed in $K$. If $K_c\ne1$, then, for every $1\ne h\in K_c$, \[ K_c=C_K(h)=N_K(K_c). \] Thus two nontrivial cut stabilizers either are equal or have trivial intersection. For the finite-parameter tree $T$ of Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree}, if $C$ is such a nontrivial stabilizer, the fixed-point poset $T^C$ is nonempty and has weakly contractible nerve. Every point fixed by one nonidentity element of $C$ has stabilizer exactly $C$.
notes: Proved: root closure and maximal cut stabilizers

statement: In the notation of Proposition~\ref{G:treedoublemodel}, let $\mathscr C$ be the set of distinct nontrivial groups $K_c$ for $c\in T$. It is an $H=K\rtimes G$-set under conjugation. Choose one $C$ from every $H$-orbit, and put \[ A_{\mathrm{cut}}=\bigoplus_{[C]\in\mathscr C/H}C, \qquad X=|(NS)/G|,\qquad Y=|NT/H|,\qquad\Gamma=K_G. \] The degree-one stabilizer row in (TD.3) has zero homology in positive horizontal degrees, and has $H_0=A_{\mathrm{cut}}$. Via the two projections of the double model, there are natural isomorphisms \[ H_i(X;\Z)\cong H_i(Y;\Z)\quad(i\ge3) \] and a natural exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow H_2(X;\Z)\longrightarrow H_2(Y;\Z) \stackrel{d_2}{\longrightarrow} A_{\mathrm{cut}} \longrightarrow\Gamma_{\ab} \longrightarrow H_1(Y;\Z)\longrightarrow0. \tag{TR.1} \] The map from each summand $C$ to $\Gamma_{\ab}$ is the inclusion into $K$, followed by the group-coinvariant map and abelianization. Neither $H_i(Y)$ nor the transgression $d_2$ is declared zero. In particular the remaining general $H_2(X)$ question is exactly the kernel of the displayed transgression.
notes: Proved: collapse of the stabilizer row

statement: There is an explicit diagram $M:\Cdelta\to\FreeMon$ of finite-rank free monoids with injective transition maps for which $T_i(M_{\ab})=0$ for every $i>0$, but a nontrivial cut stabilizer $K_c$ of its smooth limit monoid maps noninjectively to $K_G$. For this example, in Corollary~\ref{G:stabilizerrow}, \[ H_2(X;\Z)=0,\qquad H_2(Y;\Z)\ne0,\qquad d_2\ne0. \] Thus neither cut-group injectivity nor vanishing of the quotient $Y$'s second homology is a valid general shortcut. The example does not refute injectivity of $d_2$; here that differential is injective.
notes: Proved: cut groups can die in coinvariants

statement: Let $G=\Aut(M_0)$ for $\Cdelta$. Fix a strong $E\subseteq F$, an embedding $\eta:E\to M_0$, a strong flag \[ E=B_0\subsetneq B_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq B_d=F, \qquad B_j=\operatorname{cl}_F(B_{j-1}\cup\{a_j\}), \] and signs $\epsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$. Give the set $\Omega$ of strong embeddings $f:F\to M_0$ extending $\eta$ its signed lexicographic order from this flag. If $D\subset M_0$ is finite strong and contains $\eta E$, every $G_D$-invariant initial segment of $\Omega$ is a union of cells in the following finite convex partition: \begin{enumerate} \item for $0\le j<d$, each strong $h:B_j\to D$ extending $\eta$, and each raw-order gap $I$ of $D$, the nonempty set \[ \{f\in\Omega:f|_{B_j}=h,\ f(a_{j+1})\in I\}; \tag{OC.1} \] \item the singleton sets consisting of strong embeddings $F\to D$ extending $\eta$. \end{enumerate} In particular membership is expressible using only equalities between the displayed support coordinates and strict raw-order comparisons with the finitely many points of $D$.
notes: Proved: smooth cuts in a support lexicographic order

statement: Let $L$ be a smooth $G$-set with a $G$-invariant partial order whose principal downsets are chains. Identify each of finitely many chosen orbits with $\operatorname{Emb}(F_i,M_0)$ using its unique finite strong support. On this finite union of orbits, every comparison $x\preceq y$ is given by a finite Boolean combination of equalities and raw-order comparisons between the coordinates of the two support embeddings. No relation on the union of the supports other than raw order and coordinate equality is needed in these formulas. More precisely, let $E_i\subseteq F_i$ be the component base of the $i$th orbit from Theorem~\ref{G:alltreeorders}. If a point of orbit $i$ lies below a point of orbit $j$, its component label is obtained from the latter's component label by a fixed strong embedding $E_i\to E_j$. If this embedding is an isomorphism, each matched pair of orbit components has a linearly ordered union. Consequently a matched pair of components linked by a comparison has a chain union unless the indicated inclusion of component bases is strict. No assertion is made about incomparable components of the same base type. This applies, in particular, to the rooted tree order on the completion $T$ of Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree}, rooted at the $G$-fixed original vertex $1$.
notes: Proved: comparisons between finitely many smooth orbits use only order

statement: Let $A$ be a nonempty connected small category in $\mathcal F$, let $L:A\to\Set$ be any covariant set action, and let $B$ be a nonempty connected component of $\operatorname{El}_A(L)$. Then $B\in\mathcal F$. No finiteness of hom-sets or of the sets $L(a)$ is required. More generally, if $u:A\to D$ is an ordinary final functor, then $D\in\mathcal F$. There is a separate degreewise assertion, not requiring $A\in\mathcal F$: fix $i>0$ and a commutative ring $R$. If \[ L_i\colim_A\bigl(R\otimes_{\Z}M_{\ab}\bigr)=0 \quad\text{for every }M:A\to\FreeMon, \] then the same assertion holds with $B$ in place of $A$. The zero ring is allowed.
notes: Proved: free-monoid tests pass to action components

statement: Let $J$ be a small category with finite hom-sets and a degree function $d:\operatorname{Ob}J\to\N$ such that every nonidentity arrow strictly increases degree and there are only finitely many objects of each bounded degree. Let $N:J\to\Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ have finite-dimensional values. There is a diagram $L:J\to\Ab$ of finite-rank free abelian groups, with a specified basis at every object, such that \[ L\otimes_{\Z}\Q\cong\underline\Q\oplus N \tag{PM.1} \] naturally, and every nonidentity transition matrix of $L$ has strictly positive integer entries. If all transitions of $N$ are injective, those of $L$ can also be chosen injective. In particular there is such an injective strictly-positive-matrix diagram on $\Cdelta$ for which \[ T_1(L)\otimes\Q\cong\Q. \] This is a statement about positive integer matrices. It does not assert that they can be realized by a functor to free monoids.
notes: Proved: positive integral stabilization

statement: The amalgamation property fails for finite-rank free monoids with injective substitutions whose basis images are bifix codes, even when both induced group maps are isomorphisms and their positive abelianized matrices are identical. Put \[ H=\FreeMon(x,y,z),\quad P=\FreeMon(a,b,c),\quad Q=\FreeMon(A,B,C), \] and define $i:H\to P$, $j:H\to Q$ by \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &x&y&z\\\hline i&bacb&bcacb&ccacb\\ j&BABC&BCABC&CCABC. \end{array} \tag{BF.1} \] Both maps are injective with bifix basis images, both group maps are isomorphisms, and their abelianized matrices are \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\2&2&1\\1&2&3\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det=1. \tag{BF.2} \] Nevertheless there are no injective monoid maps $u:P\to S$, $v:Q\to S$ into any locally free monoid $S$ with $ui=vj$.
notes: Refuted: cone-compatible bifix free-factor amalgamation

statement: Let $S$ be a locally free monoid, $K=S^{\gp}$, and give $K$ the prefix order. Suppose $1\ne g\in S$ and $y\in K$ satisfy $g^n\le y$ for every integer $n\ge0$. In the bounded Dedekind--MacNeille completion, \[ \sup_{n\ge0} g^n=y\wedge gy. \] The vertices $y$ and $gy$ are incomparable, and their displayed meet is nonprincipal and is fixed by $g$. Consequently every nontrivial stabilizer of an arbitrary bounded Dedekind--MacNeille cut occurs as the stabilizer of a cut obtained by one bounded meet or one bounded join of two original vertices, up to left translation. The original cut need not itself have finite parameters. If $S$ carries a smooth group action, each of these finite witnesses is smooth.
notes: Proved: bounded powers have a finite cut witness

statement: Let $G$ be the group of $\Cdelta$, let $S$ be a smooth locally free $G$-monoid, and put $K=S^{\gp}$ and $H=K\rtimes G$. Let $T$ be the finite-parameter tree of Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree}, and let $\widehat T$ be the set of all bounded Dedekind--MacNeille cuts whose $G$-stabilizer is open. Then $\widehat T$ is an $H$-invariant smooth median pretree, with the same ordered-interval path construction as $T$. Every fixed-point nerve $(N\widehat T)^U$ is weakly contractible when $U\le G$; the analogous assertion holds for any subgroup of $H$ having a fixed vertex. The sets of nontrivial $K$-stabilizers occurring on $T$ and $\widehat T$ are equal. The natural inclusion induces a weak equivalence \[ |NT/H|\ \longrightarrow\ |N\widehat T/H|. \] Consequently the double model and the transgression exact sequence of Proposition~\ref{G:treedoublemodel} and Corollary~\ref{G:stabilizerrow} may use all smooth bounded cuts, with the same stabilizer summands. This does not assert that the transgression is injective or that its source vanishes.
notes: Proved: all smooth bounded cuts give the same quotient model

statement: Let $G$ be the group of $\Cdelta$. Let $L$ be a smooth $G$-set equipped with an invariant rooted-tree order $\preceq$: it has a $G$-fixed least point $r$, every principal downset is a chain, and every pair has a greatest common predecessor $x\wedge_r y$. Then \[ G_x\subseteq G_{x\wedge_r y} \quad\hbox{or}\quad G_y\subseteq G_{x\wedge_r y}. \] Equivalently, the unique finite strong support of the rooted meet is contained in the support of one input. For each fixed pair of input orbits, partition its pairs by the raw order and equality pattern of their finite support coordinates. On each nonempty part, the meet is an equivariant function of one of the two inputs alone. In particular there are only finitely many meet-output orbits. The closure of a finite union of $G$-orbits under rooted meets is again a finite union of $G$-orbits. For the canonical tree $T$ of Proposition~\ref{G:prefixtree}, or its smooth completion $\widehat T$ in Proposition~\ref{G:smooth-cut-completion}, every finite union of $G$-orbits is contained in a $G$-invariant subposet with finitely many $G$-orbits that contains $1$, all rooted meets, and all turns of the canonical paths between its vertices. Its nerve in the original prefix orientation is weakly contractible. These subposets form a directed family whose union is the whole tree. The same assertions hold relative to an open pointwise stabilizer $G_B$. In particular, consider a finite direct category and a strictly commutative diagram of copies of $T$ (or $\widehat T$), all arrow maps being left translations by specified elements of $K$. At each object prescribe finitely many vertices. There is one open $U=G_B$ and a subdiagram containing these vertices whose object values are weakly contractible, turn-closed subposets with finitely many $U$-orbits. This is a finite-orbit tree-hull assertion. It does not supply a model over an exact indexing category, or compatibility of these hulls with all left $K$-translations and monoid products.
notes: Proved: rooted meets do not enlarge both input supports

statement: Let $E\le F,D$ be finite strong objects of $\Cdelta$, fix an embedding of $E$ in $M_0$, and let $\Omega_F,\Omega_D$ be the sets of strong embeddings extending it. Give these sets the signed lexicographic orders determined by flags \[ E=A_0\subsetneq A_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq A_d=F, \quad A_i=\operatorname{cl}_F(A_{i-1}\cup\{a_i\}), \quad \epsilon_i\in\{+1,-1\}, \] and \[ E=B_0\subsetneq B_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq B_e=D, \quad B_i=\operatorname{cl}_D(B_{i-1}\cup\{b_i\}), \quad \eta_i\in\{+1,-1\}. \] Suppose $f\mapsto C_f$ is a $G_E$-equivariant map from $\Omega_F$ to initial segments of $\Omega_D$, monotone for inclusion. Then it is constantly empty, constantly full, or has one of the following finite boundary descriptions. There is a common initial flag of length $j$: strong isomorphisms $h_i:B_i\to A_i$, fixing $E$, compatible under restriction, with $h_i(b_i)=a_i$ and $\eta_i=\epsilon_i$ for $1\le i\le j$. The boundary of $C_f$ follows the target prefix $f h_j$, and then either: \begin{enumerate} \item it is immediately before or immediately after the entire fiber of extensions of $f h_j$; here $j\ge1$, and when $j=e$ the fiber is a single point; or \item $j<d,e$, $\eta_{j+1}=\epsilon_{j+1}$, and its next threshold is $f(a_{j+1})$ in the $b_{j+1}$-coordinate. In this case $B_{j+1}$ and $A_{j+1}$ are not isomorphic over the identified preceding stage and distinguished new pivot. Consequently no actual source and target embeddings with that preceding prefix can have equal next pivots. \end{enumerate} In the second case the source and target next pivots lie in the same raw-order gap of the common preceding stage. The descriptions include all target points lexicographically before the specified prefix, with inequalities reversed at the negative signs. The choice of before/after and all the identifications are fixed, independent of $f$.
notes: Proved: monotone cuts follow a common initial flag
